objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3 sqlite3;
objects.description: Opaque database connection handle representing an open SQLite database. Constructed by sqlite3_open(), sqlite3_open16(), or sqlite3_open_v2(). Destroyed by sqlite3_close() or sqlite3_close_v2(). Many APIs take sqlite3* as the first parameter.

OS interface handle for an open file within a VFS implementation. pMethods points to an sqlite3_io_methods that implements I/O for this file. Typically embedded as first field of a VFS-specific subclass.
Virtual method table defining VFS file operations for an sqlite3_file. VFS implementations populate this for their file handles. iVersion gates availability of methods (v1..v3).
Virtual File System object linking SQLite core to OS. Contains methods for file and dynamic loading operations. Registered via sqlite3_vfs_register() and found via sqlite3_vfs_find().

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_mutex sqlite3_mutex;
objects.description: Opaque mutex handle used by SQLite for internal and optional external synchronization. Allocated by sqlite3_mutex_alloc() and freed by sqlite3_mutex_free().

Table of function pointers exposing the SQLite C API to loadable extensions. Provided to an extension entry point. Used with sqlite3ext.h macro redirections. Do not construct directly; SQLite populates when loading extensions.

objects.definition: typedef const char *sqlite3_filename;
objects.description: Alias type used when passing filenames (possibly URIs) to VFS-related APIs. It is a const char* pointer type.
Pluggable memory allocator methods structure used with sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_MALLOC/GETMALLOC). Supplies malloc/realloc/free/size/roundup and init/shutdown hooks.

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_stmt sqlite3_stmt;
objects.description: Opaque prepared statement object representing compiled SQL. Created by sqlite3_prepare_v2/v3 (or UTF-16 variants) and finalized by sqlite3_finalize(). Stepped via sqlite3_step().

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_value sqlite3_value;
objects.description: Dynamically typed SQL value container used in function arguments, VTab RHS values, and column_value(). May be protected or unprotected. Use sqlite3_value_xxx accessors. Duplicated by sqlite3_value_dup() and freed by sqlite3_value_free().

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_context sqlite3_context;
objects.description: Opaque execution context passed to SQL function callbacks. Used to set results and access user data. The context is managed by SQLite during function invocation.

Base instance structure for a virtual table implementation. Embedded and extended by module code. Holds a pointer to its sqlite3_module, a refcount of open cursors, and an error message buffer. VTab lifecycle controlled by module xCreate/xConnect/xDisconnect/xDestroy and SQLite.
Base cursor type for virtual table iteration. Implementations extend with their own fields. Lifecycle via module xOpen/xClose and used with xFilter/xNext/xEof/xColumn/xRowid.
Virtual table module method table. Implementations register one per vtab module via sqlite3_create_module(_v2). iVersion gates optional methods (savepoints, shadow name, integrity).

Structure passed to xBestIndex for vtab query planning. Contains incoming WHERE/ORDER BY info and space for module to describe its chosen plan (constraints usage, index id/string, ordering, cost/rows, flags).

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_pcache sqlite3_pcache;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a custom page cache instance used with sqlite3_pcache_methods2. Allocated via xCreate and freed via xDestroy in methods table.
Represents a single page in a custom page cache. pBuf is the page storage, pExtra is per-page extra area sized by cache setup.
Obsolete custom page cache methods (pre-3.6) retained for compatibility. Prefer sqlite3_pcache_methods2.
Modern custom page cache provider API. Register via sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_PCACHE2/GETPCACHE2). Provides page fetch/unpin/rekey/truncate and cache sizing. iVersion currently 1.

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_backup sqlite3_backup;
objects.description: Opaque handle for an online backup operation. Created by sqlite3_backup_init(), stepped via sqlite3_backup_step(), finished by sqlite3_backup_finish().
Context passed to an rtree geometry callback registered via sqlite3_rtree_geometry_callback(). Holds parameters and user data for the geometry test.
Extended context for rtree 2nd-generation query callbacks (sqlite3_rtree_query_callback). Provides access to node/entry coordinates, levels, and allows returning a score and within flag.

Function table provided to FTS5 extension functions (auxiliary functions) to inspect the current match context, tokenize text, access columns, phrase hits, etc. iVersion controls availability of newer methods.

objects.definition: typedef struct Fts5Context Fts5Context;
objects.description: Opaque handle passed to FTS5 auxiliary functions representing the current match row and query context. Used only with Fts5ExtensionApi methods.
Iterator state used with Fts5ExtensionApi xPhraseFirst/Next APIs to walk phrase occurrences or columns. Treated as opaque by extensions.

Tokenizer vtable for FTS5 custom tokenizers (v2 preferred, legacy fts5_tokenizer also shown). Provides create/delete/tokenize methods. Registered via fts5_api->xCreateTokenizer_v2 (or xCreateTokenizer).

objects.definition: typedef struct Fts5Tokenizer Fts5Tokenizer;
objects.description: Opaque tokenizer instance allocated by an FTS5 tokenizer implementation. Passed back to xDelete and xTokenize.

Entry-point API passed to FTS5 extensions (from fts5=1 virtual table). Used to register custom tokenizers and auxiliary functions and to query existing tokenizers. iVersion governs availability of *_v2 methods.

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_str sqlite3_str;
objects.description: Opaque dynamic string builder object. Created by sqlite3_str_new(), appended via sqlite3_str_* APIs, and finished by sqlite3_str_finish() which returns a malloced char*.

functions.name: sqlite3_libversion
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a static UTF-8 string containing the SQLite library version (e.g., "3.51.1"). Intended for comparing the runtime library version with compiled headers.
requirements: Must not free or modify the returned string pointer; it is managed by SQLite.
Thread-safe to call at any time.

functions.name: sqlite3_sourceid
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a static string with the SQLite source ID for this library build (timestamp and SCM hash). Useful for diagnostics and verifying library provenance.
requirements: Do not free or modify the returned pointer.
Thread-safe to call at any time.

functions.name: sqlite3_libversion_number
functions.description: Returns the numeric SQLite library version as an integer (X*1000000 + Y*1000 + Z). Use for version comparisons without string parsing.
requirements: No parameters required; thread-safe.

functions.name: sqlite3_compileoption_used
functions.description: Returns 1 if the named compile-time option (with or without SQLITE_ prefix) was used to build the library, 0 otherwise.
requirements: zOptName must be a valid null-terminated C string.
If built with SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS, this function always returns 0.

functions.name: sqlite3_compileoption_get
functions.description: Returns the N-th compile-time option string (without SQLITE_ prefix) or NULL if N is out of range. Iterate with N=0.. until NULL.
requirements: N must be >= 0; iteration ends at NULL.
Returned string is managed by SQLite; do not free.
If built with SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS, returns NULL for all N.

functions.name: sqlite3_threadsafe
functions.description: Returns the compile-time setting of SQLITE_THREADSAFE (0,1,2). Indicates if the library was built with mutexes enabled. Does not reflect runtime changes from sqlite3_config().
requirements: No initialization required; may be called anytime.

functions.name: sqlite3_close
functions.description: Closes and destroys a database connection and deallocates associated resources. Fails with SQLITE_BUSY if there are unfinalized statements, open blobs, or unfinished backups.
requirements: Argument must be either NULL (no-op) or a valid sqlite3* returned by sqlite3_open[_v2|16]() that has not been previously closed.
Caller must finalize all prepared statements, close blobs, and finish backups before calling to avoid SQLITE_BUSY.
Safe to call with NULL (no-op).

functions.name: sqlite3_close
functions.description: Destructor for an sqlite3 database connection. Closes the open database handle and frees associated resources. Returns SQLITE_OK on success, or SQLITE_BUSY if there are still unfinalized prepared statements, open blob handles, or unfinished backups. Calling with NULL is a no-op.
requirements: The argument must be either NULL or a valid sqlite3* returned by sqlite3_open(), sqlite3_open16(), or sqlite3_open_v2().
All prepared statements must be finalized, blob handles closed, and sqlite3_backup objects finished before calling, otherwise SQLITE_BUSY is returned and the connection remains open.
If a transaction is open when the connection is destroyed, it is rolled back automatically.
Do not call after it has already been closed.

functions.name: sqlite3_close_v2
functions.description: Marks the database connection for closure and returns SQLITE_OK even if there are unfinalized statements, open blobs, or backups. The connection becomes a zombie and is automatically deallocated when dependent objects are finalized/closed.
requirements: Argument must be NULL or a valid, open sqlite3*.
Order of cleanup can be arbitrary in GC languages; ensure no further API calls on the zombie connection.
Calling with NULL is a no-op.

functions.name: sqlite3_close_v2
functions.description: Deferred-destructor for an sqlite3 database connection. If there are unfinalized statements or open blobs/backups, marks the connection as a zombie and defers final deallocation until they are all closed/finalized. Returns SQLITE_OK even if deferring. Designed for garbage-collected host languages.
requirements: The argument must be either NULL or a valid sqlite3* obtained from an open call and not previously closed.
Calling with NULL is a no-op.
Statements/blobs/backups can remain open; the connection becomes unusable and is freed automatically once they are all cleaned up.

functions.name: sqlite3_exec
functions.signature: int sqlite3_exec(sqlite3*, const char *sql, int (*callback)(void*,int,char**,char**), void *, char **errmsg);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to prepare, step, and finalize one or more semicolon-separated SQL statements on an open database. Optionally invokes a callback per result row.
requirements: Database handle must be valid and remain open for duration of call.
SQL string must remain unmodified during execution.
If callback is non-NULL, it must tolerate being called with column count and arrays of UTF-8 strings (NULL pointers for SQL NULL).
Must not dereference callback arrays after returning from callback.
If errmsg is non-NULL and an error occurs, caller must free *errmsg using sqlite3_free().
If the callback returns non-zero, sqlite3_exec aborts with SQLITE_ABORT.

functions.name: sqlite3_initialize
functions.description: Explicitly initializes the SQLite library and its OS interface. Normally not required, as many APIs autoinitialize unless compiled with SQLITE_OMIT_AUTOINIT.
requirements: Thread-safe to call; effective only on first call since last shutdown.
Returns SQLITE_OK on success or an error code if initialization fails.

functions.name: sqlite3_initialize
functions.description: Explicitly initializes the SQLite library and underlying OS-specific layers. Normally unnecessary unless SQLite is compiled without auto-init. Returns SQLITE_OK on success.
requirements: May be called multiple times; only the first effective call performs initialization.
Thread-safe.
If compiled with SQLITE_OMIT_AUTOINIT, applications should call this before any other SQLite API.

functions.name: sqlite3_shutdown
functions.description: Shuts down the SQLite library, deallocating global resources. Not threadsafe—must be called from a single thread with all DB connections closed and SQLite resources deallocated.
requirements: Must not be called concurrently with other SQLite APIs; use only when no other threads are using SQLite.
All database connections must be closed and SQLite resources freed before calling.

functions.name: sqlite3_shutdown
functions.description: Shuts down SQLite, deallocating global resources allocated since sqlite3_initialize(). Not thread-safe; must be called from a single thread.
requirements: Must be called only when all database connections are closed and SQLite resources have been released.
Call from a single thread; not thread-safe.
Only the first effective call after a corresponding initialize() performs deinitialization.

functions.name: sqlite3_os_init
functions.description: Performs OS-specific initialization for SQLite VFS. Intended to be called internally by sqlite3_initialize().
requirements: Applications should not call directly except in custom builds (SQLITE_OS_OTHER); must return SQLITE_OK on success.

functions.name: sqlite3_os_init
functions.description: Performs OS-specific initialization of SQLite (VFS setup etc.). Called internally by sqlite3_initialize(); applications should not call directly except in custom builds.
requirements: Applications should not invoke directly; use sqlite3_initialize().
In custom builds (SQLITE_OS_OTHER), the application-supplied implementation must return SQLITE_OK on success or an error code on failure.

functions.name: sqlite3_os_end
functions.description: Performs OS-specific shutdown tasks for SQLite VFS. Intended to be called by sqlite3_shutdown().
requirements: Applications should not call directly except in custom builds; must return SQLITE_OK on success.

functions.name: sqlite3_os_end
functions.description: Undoes OS-specific initialization performed by sqlite3_os_init(). Called internally by sqlite3_shutdown().
requirements: Applications should not call directly; use sqlite3_shutdown().
In custom builds (SQLITE_OS_OTHER), the application-supplied implementation must return SQLITE_OK on success or an error code on failure.

functions.name: sqlite3_config
functions.description: Global library configuration API to tune SQLite behavior (mutexes, memory, logging, etc.). Some options are only valid before sqlite3_initialize() or after sqlite3_shutdown().
requirements: Not threadsafe; ensure no other SQLite interfaces are called concurrently.
Most options must be set before initialization (or after shutdown).
Passing an unsupported or discontinued option returns non-zero error code.
Arguments and types must match the chosen configuration verb.

functions.name: sqlite3_config
functions.description: Global SQLite library configuration. Must be invoked before sqlite3_initialize() (or after sqlite3_shutdown()), except for specific anytime options. Configures memory allocators, mutexes, logging, page-cache, threading modes, etc. Returns SQLITE_OK on success or an error code.
requirements: Not thread-safe; ensure no SQLite APIs are running concurrently.
Must be called before sqlite3_initialize() or after sqlite3_shutdown(), except for documented anytime options (e.g., SQLITE_CONFIG_LOG, SQLITE_CONFIG_PCACHE_HDRSZ).
Arguments and types depend on the first verb; caller must pass correct types.
Passing an unsupported or deprecated option returns a non-zero error code.
If used as part of sqlite3_os_init() implementation, ensure ordering constraints are respected.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_config
functions.description: Configures a single database connection (lookaside memory, pragmas, capabilities).
requirements: Database handle must be valid.
Varargs types must match the selected verb (see SQLITE_DBCONFIG_*).
Returns SQLITE_OK if and only if the change is accepted.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_config
functions.description: Per-connection configuration changes. Adjusts behavior of a specific sqlite3 connection (lookaside, foreign keys, triggers, views, tokenizer, load_extension, etc.). Returns SQLITE_OK if and only if successful.
requirements: The first argument must be a valid open sqlite3*.
The second verb and trailing arguments must match the documented signature for that verb.
Some verbs require the connection to be in a specific state (e.g., lookaside only when not in use).
Returns SQLITE_BUSY if trying to change lookaside while lookaside memory is in use.

functions.name: sqlite3_extended_result_codes
functions.description: Enables (onoff!=0) or disables (onoff=0) extended result codes on a connection to get richer error info from APIs like sqlite3_step().
requirements: Valid sqlite3* handle.
Takes effect immediately for subsequent API error returns.

functions.name: sqlite3_last_insert_rowid
functions.description: Returns the rowid of the most recent successful INSERT into a rowid table or virtual table on the given connection, or 0 if none. Value may be affected by triggers and OR REPLACE logic.
requirements: Valid sqlite3* handle.
Concurrent inserts on same connection can make the value unpredictable if called concurrently; use connection-level serialization if required.

functions.name: sqlite3_set_last_insert_rowid
functions.description: Sets the connection’s last-insert rowid to a specific value without inserting a row (e.g., to mask virtual table internal inserts).
requirements: Valid sqlite3* handle.
Does not validate that the rowid actually exists.

functions.name: sqlite3_changes
functions.description: Returns the number of database rows changed, inserted, or deleted by the most recent INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE on the connection, excluding changes from triggers and foreign key actions.
requirements: Valid sqlite3* handle.
Value undefined if count exceeds INT max; use sqlite3_changes64() for large counts.
Reading during triggers returns count for current statement; preserved over nested triggers.

functions.name: sqlite3_changes64
functions.description: 64-bit version of sqlite3_changes(). Returns total rows modified by last DML statement on the connection.
requirements: Valid sqlite3* handle.

functions.name: sqlite3_total_changes
functions.description: Returns total number of rows inserted, modified, or deleted by all DML statements since the connection was opened, including those in triggers, excluding REPLACE deletes.
requirements: Valid sqlite3* handle.
Undefined if total exceeds INT max; use sqlite3_total_changes64() for large totals.

functions.name: sqlite3_total_changes64
functions.description: 64-bit total changes counter for the connection.
requirements: Valid sqlite3* handle.

functions.name: sqlite3_interrupt
functions.description: Requests that ongoing operations on the database connection abort at the earliest opportunity with SQLITE_INTERRUPT. Affects currently running and subsequently started statements until all running statements complete.
requirements: Valid sqlite3* handle that will remain valid until the call returns.
May be called from a different thread than the executing statement, but the connection must not be closed during the call.

functions.name: sqlite3_is_interrupted
functions.description: Returns 1 if an interrupt is currently in effect for the connection due to sqlite3_interrupt(), 0 otherwise.
requirements: Valid sqlite3* handle.

functions.name: sqlite3_is_interrupted
functions.description: Returns 1 if an interrupt (sqlite3_interrupt) is currently in effect for the database connection, else 0.

functions.name: sqlite3_complete
functions.description: Returns 1 if the given UTF-8 SQL text appears to form a complete statement (ends with semicolon token not within quotes/comments and is not a CREATE TRIGGER prefix), 0 if incomplete, or SQLITE_NOMEM on OOM.
requirements: sql must be a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string.
Does not validate syntax correctness—only checks completeness.

functions.name: sqlite3_complete16
functions.description: UTF-16 (native byte order) equivalent of sqlite3_complete(). May auto-initialize SQLite.
requirements: sql must be a NUL-terminated UTF-16 string in native byte order.
May return non-zero if auto-initialization fails, regardless of completeness.

functions.name: sqlite3_busy_handler
functions.description: Registers a busy-handler callback invoked when a table/database is locked. The handler decides whether to retry (non-zero) or abort (zero). Setting a new handler replaces any existing or busy_timeout handler.
requirements: Valid sqlite3* handle.
Callback must be non-reentrant and must not perform operations that modify the same database connection; doing so is undefined.
Set to NULL to disable custom handler.
Busy handler may not be invoked to avoid deadlocks in some contention scenarios.

functions.name: sqlite3_busy_timeout
functions.description: Sets a default busy-handler that sleeps and retries until at least ms milliseconds of total sleep time have elapsed. Pass ms<=0 to disable busy handlers.
requirements: Valid sqlite3* handle.
Replaces any previously set busy handler on the connection.

functions.name: sqlite3_setlk_timeout
functions.signature: int sqlite3_setlk_timeout(sqlite3*, int ms, int flags);
functions.description: Configures setlk (blocking lock) timeout on VFSes that support it (SQLITE_ENABLE_SETLK_TIMEOUT builds). Only affects eligible locks on WAL databases. Optionally pass SQLITE_SETLK_BLOCK_ON_CONNECT to block on SHARED lock when connecting to WAL.
requirements: Only meaningful if compiled with SQLITE_ENABLE_SETLK_TIMEOUT and the VFS supports blocking locks; otherwise it is a no-op returning SQLITE_OK.
Pass 0 to disable blocking locks; -1 to block indefinitely; other negative values undefined.
Call after sqlite3_busy_timeout() if configuring different busy and setlk timeouts.

functions.name: sqlite3_get_table
functions.signature: int sqlite3_get_table(sqlite3 *db, const char *zSql, char ***pazResult, int *pnRow, int *pnColumn, char **pzErrmsg);
functions.description: Legacy convenience API to execute SQL and return a result table as an array of char* (column names followed by row data). Use sqlite3_exec() instead for new code.
requirements: db must be a valid open connection.
On success, caller must free the result using sqlite3_free_table().
If pzErrmsg is non-NULL and error occurs, *pzErrmsg must be freed by caller using sqlite3_free().
Not safe for very large result sets due to memory usage.

functions.name: sqlite3_free_table
functions.description: Frees the result table allocated by sqlite3_get_table(). Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: Pass exactly the pointer returned in *pazResult from sqlite3_get_table().
Do not use the result after freeing.

functions.name: sqlite3_mprintf
functions.description: SQLite-managed malloc formatting function similar to printf(), returns a heap-allocated UTF-8 string. Free with sqlite3_free(). Supports SQLite-specific format specifiers.
requirements: Returns NULL on OOM; caller must check and free with sqlite3_free().
Format string must be valid per SQLite printf rules.

functions.name: sqlite3_vmprintf
functions.description: va_list variant of sqlite3_mprintf().
requirements: Same as sqlite3_mprintf(); free returned string with sqlite3_free().

functions.name: sqlite3_snprintf
functions.description: SQLite variant of snprintf(). Writes formatted string into provided buffer of size n (including NUL) and returns zBuf. Guarantees NUL termination if n>0.
requirements: zBuf must point to a buffer of at least n bytes.
Return is pointer to buffer; does not report number of characters written.

functions.name: sqlite3_vsnprintf
functions.signature: char *sqlite3_vsnprintf(int n, char *zBuf, const char *zFormat, va_list);
functions.description: va_list variant of sqlite3_snprintf().
requirements: Same buffer and size requirements as sqlite3_snprintf().

functions.name: sqlite3_malloc
functions.description: Allocates at least N bytes using SQLite’s memory allocator. Returns NULL on failure or if N<=0.
requirements: Returned memory must be freed with sqlite3_free() or resized with sqlite3_realloc().
Avoid mixing with system malloc/free.

functions.name: sqlite3_malloc64
functions.description: 64-bit size variant of sqlite3_malloc().
requirements: Free with sqlite3_free().

functions.name: sqlite3_realloc
functions.description: Resizes a prior allocation from sqlite3_malloc()/realloc()/malloc64(). If X is NULL, behaves like sqlite3_malloc(). If N<=0, frees X and returns NULL.
requirements: Pointer must be from SQLite’s allocator or NULL.
On failure returns NULL and leaves original allocation intact.

functions.name: sqlite3_realloc64
functions.description: 64-bit size variant of sqlite3_realloc().
requirements: Pointer must be from SQLite's allocator or NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_free
functions.description: Frees memory obtained from SQLite allocation APIs. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: Do not free memory not allocated by SQLite.

functions.name: sqlite3_msize
functions.description: Returns the size of a memory allocation previously obtained from SQLite memory APIs. Returns 0 if X is NULL. Behavior is undefined if X is not a valid current allocation.
requirements: Pointer must be a current allocation from SQLite’s allocator or NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_memory_used
functions.description: Returns current number of bytes of heap memory outstanding in SQLite’s allocation subsystem (if memstatus enabled).
requirements: Requires SQLITE_CONFIG_MEMSTATUS enabled (default unless compiled otherwise).

functions.name: sqlite3_memory_highwater
functions.description: Returns the high-water mark of sqlite3_memory_used(). If resetFlag is true, resets the high-water mark to current usage before returning the previous high.
requirements: Memstatus must be enabled; otherwise returns 0.

functions.name: sqlite3_randomness
functions.description: Fills buffer P with N bytes of pseudo-random data from SQLite’s PRNG. If not seeded yet, seeds from VFS xRandomness.
requirements: P may be NULL; in that case nothing is written.
Provide sufficient buffer size of at least N bytes.

functions.name: sqlite3_set_authorizer
functions.signature: int sqlite3_set_authorizer(sqlite3*, int (*xAuth)(void*,int,const char*,const char*,const char*,const char*), void *pUserData);
functions.description: Registers an authorization callback invoked during statement compilation to approve/deny SQL actions. Return SQLITE_OK to allow, SQLITE_DENY to abort with error, or SQLITE_IGNORE to modify behavior in limited cases (e.g., column read yields NULL).
requirements: Valid sqlite3* handle.
Callback must not modify the database connection (including preparing or stepping statements); doing so is undefined.
Set NULL to disable authorizer.
Must remain installed across possible reprepare during sqlite3_step().

functions.name: sqlite3_open
functions.description: Opens (and possibly creates) a database file using UTF-8 filename. On success writes a database handle to *ppDb and returns SQLITE_OK. On failure returns an error code and usually populates *ppDb with a connection that can return an error message.
requirements: filename must be UTF-8; ":memory:" creates private in-memory DB; empty string creates temp DB.
Caller must close *ppDb with sqlite3_close/_v2 when done.
Not all flags are available—use sqlite3_open_v2 for more control.

functions.name: sqlite3_open16
functions.description: UTF-16 (native endian) version of sqlite3_open().
requirements: filename must be nul-terminated UTF-16 native endian.
Close handle when done.

functions.name: sqlite3_open_v2
functions.signature: int sqlite3_open_v2(const char *filename, sqlite3 **ppDb, int flags, const char *zVfs);
functions.description: Opens a database connection with explicit flags (READONLY/READWRITE/CREATE, URI, NOMUTEX/FULLMUTEX, SHAREDCACHE/PRIVATECACHE, EXRESCODE/NOFOLLOW) and optional VFS name.
requirements: flags must include one of READONLY, READWRITE, or READWRITE|CREATE.
Close the handle with sqlite3_close/_v2.
zVfs NULL uses default VFS.
Historical behavior may ignore disallowed flags; future versions may error—avoid passing VFS-only flags.

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_parameter
functions.description: If filename z is a URI and contains query parameter zParam, returns its value as a string (empty string if present with no value); NULL if not present.
requirements: z must be a valid filename pointer from SQLite (xOpen zFilename, sqlite3_db_filename, or sqlite3_create_filename).
Do not free returned pointer; managed by SQLite.
If z is NULL or not recognized, returns NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_parameter
functions.signature: SQLITE_API const char *sqlite3_uri_parameter(sqlite3_filename z, const char *zParam);
functions.description: For a filename/URI F, returns value string for query parameter P, or NULL if not present. Empty string if parameter has no value.
requirements: F must be a filename pointer from SQLite (xOpen zName, sqlite3_db_filename, or sqlite3_create_filename).
Returned pointer valid while F remains valid.

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_boolean
functions.signature: int sqlite3_uri_boolean(sqlite3_filename z, const char *zParam, int bDefault);
functions.description: Returns interpreted boolean value of URI parameter zParam: true for yes/true/on or non-zero number; false for no/false/off or number starting with 0. Returns bDefault if not present or unrecognized.
requirements: z must be a proper SQLite filename pointer.
Case-insensitive parsing of textual values.

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_boolean
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_uri_boolean(sqlite3_filename z, const char *zParam, int bDefault);
functions.description: Returns boolean interpretation of URI parameter P of filename F: true for yes/true/on or non-zero number; false for no/false/off or 0; if absent or unrecognized returns bDefault.
requirements: F must be a valid SQLite filename pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_int64
functions.signature: sqlite3_int64 sqlite3_uri_int64(sqlite3_filename z, const char *zParam, sqlite3_int64 D);
functions.description: Returns 64-bit integer value of URI query parameter zParam or D if not present or non-integer.
requirements: z must be a proper SQLite filename pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_int64
functions.signature: SQLITE_API sqlite3_int64 sqlite3_uri_int64(sqlite3_filename, const char*, sqlite3_int64);
functions.description: Returns 64-bit integer value of URI parameter P for filename F, or D if not present or not numeric.
requirements: F must be valid filename pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_key
functions.description: Returns the name of the N-th URI query parameter key for filename z, or NULL if N is out of range. Keys are zero-based and exclude the SQLITE_ prefix.
requirements: z must be a proper SQLite filename pointer.
Do not free returned pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_key
functions.signature: SQLITE_API const char *sqlite3_uri_key(const char *zUri, int N);
functions.description: Returns the name of the N-th query parameter key from a URI F, or NULL if N out of range. N is zero-based.
requirements: zUri must be a URI recognized by SQLite; result valid while zUri remains valid.

functions.name: sqlite3_filename_database
functions.description: Given a filename (database/journal/WAL) from SQLite, returns the main database filename path.
requirements: Pointer must be from SQLite VFS/xOpen or sqlite3_db_filename().
Undefined behavior if not a recognized file pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_filename_database
functions.description: Given an SQLite filename (db/journal/wal), returns pointer to the main database filename.
requirements: Argument must be a filename pointer supplied by SQLite (VFS xOpen/returned).
Result undefined for arbitrary strings.

functions.name: sqlite3_filename_journal
functions.description: Returns the corresponding rollback-journal filename for the given database filename pointer.
requirements: z must be a SQLite filename pointer or obtained from sqlite3_db_filename().

functions.name: sqlite3_filename_journal
functions.description: Given an SQLite filename pointer, returns the corresponding rollback journal filename.
requirements: Same as sqlite3_filename_database.

functions.name: sqlite3_filename_wal
functions.description: Returns the corresponding WAL filename for the given database filename pointer.
requirements: z must be a SQLite filename pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_filename_wal
functions.description: Given an SQLite filename pointer, returns the corresponding WAL filename.
requirements: Same as sqlite3_filename_database.

functions.name: sqlite3_database_file_object
functions.description: For a rollback or WAL journal file name passed into VFS xOpen, returns the sqlite3_file object of the main database file. Intended for VFS implementations only.
requirements: Argument must be the filename pointer passed to VFS xOpen when opening a journal/WAL with appropriate flags (MAIN_JOURNAL or WAL).
Not a general-purpose API.

functions.name: sqlite3_database_file_object
functions.description: Given a journal/WAL filename pointer passed to VFS xOpen with flag MAIN_JOURNAL or WAL, returns sqlite3_file* of the associated main database file.
requirements: Argument must be the filename pointer X passed into VFS xOpen for the journal/WAL; undefined otherwise.
For VFS implementations only.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_filename
functions.signature: sqlite3_filename sqlite3_create_filename(const char *zDatabase, const char *zJournal, const char *zWal, int nParam, const char **azParam);
functions.description: Allocates a composite filename object linking database, journal, WAL, and optional URI parameters suitable for passing to SQLite filename/URI helper APIs.
requirements: All of zDatabase, zJournal, zWal must be non-NULL (may be empty strings).
If nParam>0, azParam must point to an array of 2*nParam non-NULL key/value pointers; keys should not be empty.
Free with sqlite3_free_filename().
May return NULL on OOM.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_filename
functions.signature: SQLITE_API sqlite3_filename sqlite3_create_filename(const char *zDatabase, const char *zJournal, const char *zWal, int nParam, const char **azParam);
functions.description: Builds a managed filename object with database, journal, wal and URI parameters. Use with sqlite3_uri_* and sqlite3_filename_* APIs.
requirements: azParam is array of 2*nParam non-NULL key/value strings (keys non-empty).
None of zDatabase/zJournal/zWal may be NULL (may be empty).
Free with sqlite3_free_filename().

functions.name: sqlite3_free_filename
functions.description: Frees a filename object obtained from sqlite3_create_filename(). No-op for NULL.
requirements: Do not use the filename after freeing.
Ensure any associated VFS objects have been closed before freeing if used in xOpen.

functions.name: sqlite3_free_filename
functions.description: Frees a filename object previously returned by sqlite3_create_filename(). Safe to pass NULL.
requirements: Must not call on pointers not obtained from sqlite3_create_filename().

functions.name: sqlite3_errcode
functions.description: Returns the most recent error code for the database connection.
requirements: db must be valid. Some APIs preserve error code; others may overwrite.

functions.name: sqlite3_extended_errcode
functions.description: Returns the most recent extended error code for the database connection, even if extended result codes are disabled.
requirements: db must be valid.

functions.name: sqlite3_errmsg
functions.description: Returns a UTF-8 English-language description string for the most recent error on the connection, or NULL in some invalid UTF cases.
requirements: Pointer is managed by SQLite and may be invalidated by subsequent calls; copy if needed persistent.

functions.name: sqlite3_errmsg16
functions.description: Returns a UTF-16 (native) error message string for the most recent error.
requirements: Managed by SQLite; may be invalidated by subsequent calls.

functions.name: sqlite3_errstr
functions.description: Returns a static UTF-8 description string for the given result code or extended result code.
requirements: Do not free/modify returned string.

functions.name: sqlite3_error_offset
functions.description: Returns the byte offset (assuming UTF-8) of the token in the most recent SQL text that caused a parse error, or -1 if not applicable.
requirements: db must be valid.
For SQL compiled via v2/v3 prepare; not all errors have offsets.

functions.name: sqlite3_set_errmsg
functions.signature: int sqlite3_set_errmsg(sqlite3 *db, int errcode, const char *zErrMsg);
functions.description: Sets a connection’s current error code and message to the provided values. Intended for extensions to report errors via the core error reporting path.
requirements: db must be valid; zErrMsg may be NULL to set default message for errcode.
Returns SQLITE_OK on success, SQLITE_NOMEM on OOM, SQLITE_MISUSE if db is NULL/invalid.

functions.name: sqlite3_prepare
functions.signature: int sqlite3_prepare(sqlite3 *db, const char *zSql, int nByte, sqlite3_stmt **ppStmt, const char **pzTail);
functions.description: Legacy prepare interface to compile the first SQL statement in a UTF-8 buffer into a prepared statement. Prefer sqlite3_prepare_v2/v3.
requirements: db must be valid; zSql must point to SQL text of at least nByte bytes (if nByte>=0) or nul-terminated if nByte<0.
ppStmt must not be NULL; receives NULL if no SQL or on error.
If pzTail non-NULL, receives pointer to remaining uncompiled SQL.
Do not use the statement on non-SQLITE_OK return.

functions.name: sqlite3_prepare_v2
functions.signature: int sqlite3_prepare_v2(sqlite3 *db, const char *zSql, int nByte, sqlite3_stmt **ppStmt, const char **pzTail);
functions.description: Compiles the first SQL statement in a UTF-8 SQL text into a prepared statement with improved error propagation and auto-reprepare on schema changes. Prefer this for new code.
requirements: Same as sqlite3_prepare; statement holds a copy of the original SQL for reprepare and error reporting.
May reprepare during sqlite3_step(); keep authorizer/busy-handlers installed.

functions.name: sqlite3_prepare_v3
functions.signature: int sqlite3_prepare_v3(sqlite3 *db, const char *zSql, int nByte, unsigned int prepFlags, sqlite3_stmt **ppStmt, const char **pzTail);
functions.description: Like sqlite3_prepare_v2 with additional prepFlags (e.g., SQLITE_PREPARE_PERSISTENT, SQLITE_PREPARE_NO_VTAB, SQLITE_PREPARE_DONT_LOG).
requirements: prepFlags must be a valid bitwise OR of SQLITE_PREPARE_* flags.
Other requirements as for sqlite3_prepare_v2.

functions.name: sqlite3_prepare16
functions.signature: int sqlite3_prepare16(sqlite3 *db, const void *zSql, int nByte, sqlite3_stmt **ppStmt, const void **pzTail);
functions.description: UTF-16 version of sqlite3_prepare() (legacy). Converts to UTF-8 internally.
requirements: zSql must be UTF-16 native endian.
Prefer v2/v3 variants for better behavior.

functions.name: sqlite3_prepare16_v2
functions.signature: int sqlite3_prepare16_v2(sqlite3 *db, const void *zSql, int nByte, sqlite3_stmt **ppStmt, const void **pzTail);
functions.description: UTF-16 version of sqlite3_prepare_v2().
requirements: Same as v2; UTF-16 native endian input.

functions.name: sqlite3_prepare16_v3
functions.signature: int sqlite3_prepare16_v3(sqlite3 *db, const void *zSql, int nByte, unsigned int prepFlags, sqlite3_stmt **ppStmt, const void **pzTail);
functions.description: UTF-16 version of sqlite3_prepare_v3().
requirements: Valid prepFlags; UTF-16 native endian input.

functions.name: sqlite3_sql
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the original SQL text used to create the prepared statement (v2/v3 interfaces).
requirements: Do not free/modify returned pointer; managed by SQLite.
May be NULL for legacy prepared statements.

functions.name: sqlite3_expanded_sql
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated string with bound parameters expanded into the SQL of the statement. Free with sqlite3_free().
requirements: May return NULL on OOM or if trace disabled via SQLITE_OMIT_TRACE.
Caller must sqlite3_free() the returned buffer.

functions.name: sqlite3_normalized_sql
functions.description: If built with SQLITE_ENABLE_NORMALIZE, returns a normalized SQL string for the statement (literals replaced with placeholders).
requirements: Available only if SQLITE_ENABLE_NORMALIZE defined; otherwise may be unavailable.
Do not free returned pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_stmt_readonly
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the prepared statement does not directly modify the database file (e.g., SELECT, transaction control).
requirements: pStmt must be a valid prepared statement pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_stmt_isexplain
functions.description: Returns 1 if the statement is an EXPLAIN, or 2 if EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN, else 0.
requirements: Valid prepared statement.

functions.name: sqlite3_stmt_explain
functions.description: Changes the EXPLAIN mode of a prepared statement (0=normal,1=EXPLAIN,2=EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN). May reprepare; returns SQLITE_OK or error code.
requirements: Statement must be reset (not active) when changing mode; recommended to call sqlite3_reset() before.
Fails if statement was created with legacy sqlite3_prepare().

functions.name: sqlite3_stmt_busy
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the statement has been stepped at least once and neither sqlite3_reset() nor SQLITE_DONE has been reached.
requirements: Valid statement pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_count
functions.description: Returns the number of columns in the current result set for the prepared statement.
requirements: Valid statement pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_name
functions.description: Returns the name of the N-th column as UTF-8. Valid until next reprepare/step or finalize.
requirements: 0 <= N < sqlite3_column_count().
Do not free returned string; may be NULL on OOM.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_name16
functions.description: UTF-16 version of sqlite3_column_name().
requirements: Same index constraints; UTF-16 native endian string returned.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_database_name
functions.description: Returns the database name for the source of the N-th result column (requires SQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA).
requirements: Requires column metadata enabled at compile time.
Return may be NULL; do not free.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_database_name16
functions.description: UTF-16 version of sqlite3_column_database_name().
requirements: See UTF-8 variant.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_table_name
functions.description: Returns the table name for the source of the N-th result column (requires SQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA).
requirements: Compile-time option required; do not free returned string.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_table_name16
functions.description: UTF-16 version of sqlite3_column_table_name().
requirements: Same as UTF-8 variant.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_origin_name
functions.description: Returns the un-aliased column name (origin) for the N-th result column (requires SQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA).
requirements: 0<=N<col count; do not free; may be NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_origin_name16
functions.description: UTF-16 version of sqlite3_column_origin_name().
requirements: Same constraints.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_decltype
functions.description: Returns the declared column type of the table column underlying the N-th result column, or NULL if expression/subquery. UTF-8.
requirements: Requires metadata at prepare time; return managed by SQLite.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_decltype16
functions.description: UTF-16 version of sqlite3_column_decltype().
requirements: Same constraints.

functions.name: sqlite3_step
functions.description: Evaluates a prepared statement one step. Returns SQLITE_ROW for row retrieval, SQLITE_DONE when finished, or an error/extended code on failure. May auto-reprepare for schema changes with v2/v3 prepared statements.
requirements: Statement must be prepared; for queries, call until SQLITE_DONE. For DML, call until SQLITE_DONE.
After any return other than SQLITE_ROW, call sqlite3_reset() before reusing the statement (auto-reset may occur in modern builds; check docs).

functions.name: sqlite3_data_count
functions.description: Returns number of columns in the current row if sqlite3_step() has returned SQLITE_ROW and not yet reset/finalized; otherwise 0.
requirements: Valid statement pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_blob
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the BLOB data for column iCol of the current row. Pointer is valid until next type conversion, step, reset, or finalize. Zero-length BLOB returns non-NULL pointer; SQL NULL returns NULL.
requirements: Must only be called after sqlite3_step() returned SQLITE_ROW and before next step/reset/finalize.
Do not free returned pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_double
functions.description: Returns the column value converted to double. STRING or BLOB values are converted per documentation. NULL yields 0.0.
requirements: Valid during a row; type conversions may invalidate prior pointers.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_int
functions.description: Returns the column value converted to 32-bit int. Overflow may truncate.
requirements: Valid during current row.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_int64
functions.description: Returns the column value converted to signed 64-bit integer.
requirements: Valid during current row.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_text
functions.description: Returns UTF-8 text pointer for column. Valid until next conversion/step/reset/finalize. SQL NULL returns NULL; empty string returns non-NULL pointer to "".
requirements: Call only with a current row; do not free pointer; note conversions may invalidate previous blob/text pointers.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_text16
functions.description: UTF-16 (native endian) text version of sqlite3_column_text().
requirements: Same constraints as UTF-8.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_value
functions.description: Returns an unprotected sqlite3_value object for the column. Only safe for use with sqlite3_result_value(), sqlite3_bind_value(), or duplication; other accessors are not thread-safe for unprotected values.
requirements: Use only immediately and only with safe APIs as documented; object invalidated after next step/reset/finalize.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_bytes
functions.description: For BLOB or UTF-8 TEXT, returns number of bytes (excluding terminator). For UTF-16 TEXT returns number of bytes after conversion. For numeric, returns bytes of formatted string representation. For NULL, returns 0.
requirements: Call after forcing desired type to avoid implicit conversions that may invalidate prior pointers.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_bytes16
functions.description: Like sqlite3_column_bytes() but for UTF-16 strings.
requirements: Same precautions as sqlite3_column_bytes().

functions.name: sqlite3_column_type
functions.description: Returns the initial dynamic type of the column (SQLITE_INTEGER, FLOAT, TEXT, BLOB, NULL) before any conversions. After conversions, the value may be undefined but harmless.
requirements: Call before other type-converting accessors to get original type.

functions.name: sqlite3_finalize
functions.description: Deletes a prepared statement object, releasing all resources. Returns SQLITE_OK if the most recent evaluation had no error; otherwise returns that error code.
requirements: Safe to pass NULL (no-op).
Do not use statement after finalizing.

functions.name: sqlite3_reset
functions.description: Resets a prepared statement back to its initial state ready for re-execution, preserving current bindings. Returns SQLITE_OK or the error code from the most recent evaluation or reset-time errors.
requirements: Call before reusing statements after SQLITE_DONE/ERROR/etc.
Bindings remain; use sqlite3_clear_bindings() to clear.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_blob
functions.signature: int sqlite3_bind_blob(sqlite3_stmt*, int, const void*, int n, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Binds a BLOB parameter with n bytes to index (1-based). Destructor controls lifetime (SQLITE_STATIC, SQLITE_TRANSIENT, or custom). NULL pointer is equivalent to sqlite3_bind_null().
requirements: Index must be in 1..sqlite3_bind_parameter_count().
If destructor is SQLITE_TRANSIENT, SQLite copies the data; otherwise data must remain valid until statement is finalized or bound again.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_blob64
functions.signature: int sqlite3_bind_blob64(sqlite3_stmt*, int, const void*, sqlite3_uint64, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: 64-bit length variant of sqlite3_bind_blob().
requirements: Same as sqlite3_bind_blob(); length can exceed 2GB if limits permit.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_double
functions.description: Binds a double parameter.
requirements: Valid parameter index.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_int
functions.description: Binds a 32-bit integer parameter.
requirements: Valid parameter index.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_int64
functions.description: Binds a 64-bit integer parameter.
requirements: Valid parameter index.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_null
functions.description: Binds a SQL NULL to the given parameter index.
requirements: Valid parameter index.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_text
functions.signature: int sqlite3_bind_text(sqlite3_stmt*, int, const char*, int, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Binds a UTF-8 text parameter. If n<0, SQLite treats input as nul-terminated. Destructor controls lifetime (STATIC/TRANSIENT/custom).
requirements: Valid parameter index.
If n>=0, it must equal the byte length where a NUL would be if NUL-terminated; embedded NULs are preserved.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_text16
functions.signature: int sqlite3_bind_text16(sqlite3_stmt*, int, const void*, int, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Binds a UTF-16 (native endian) text parameter.
requirements: Same indexing and lifetime rules as sqlite3_bind_text().

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_text64
functions.signature: int sqlite3_bind_text64(sqlite3_stmt*, int, const char*, sqlite3_uint64, void(*)(void*), unsigned char encoding);
functions.description: Binds a Unicode string with explicit declared encoding (SQLITE_UTF8, SQLITE_UTF16, _LE, _BE).
requirements: encoding must be one of SQLITE_UTF8/UTF16/UTF16LE/UTF16BE.
Same lifetime rules as sqlite3_bind_text().

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_value
functions.description: Binds a sqlite3_value to a parameter. If the value is unprotected, only use with sqlite3_bind_value()/sqlite3_result_value()/sqlite3_value_dup() as documented.
requirements: Index must be valid.
If passing an unprotected sqlite3_value (e.g., from sqlite3_column_value()), only safe with this API.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_pointer
functions.signature: int sqlite3_bind_pointer(sqlite3_stmt*, int, void*, const char*, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Binds a typed pointer value (associated with type string T) to a parameter as an SQL NULL with pointer metadata retrievable by sqlite3_value_pointer(). Optional destructor called when done.
requirements: Type string should be a static/literal and consistent with consumers.
D must not be SQLITE_TRANSIENT (undefined).

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_zeroblob
functions.description: Binds a zeroblob of n bytes as a placeholder for incremental blob I/O.
requirements: n<0 results in a zero-length blob.
Index must be valid.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_zeroblob64
functions.description: 64-bit size variant of zeroblob binding.
requirements: Index must be valid.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_parameter_count
functions.description: Returns the index of the rightmost parameter (i.e., number of parameters). May exceed number of unique named parameters if using ?NNN.
requirements: Valid statement pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_parameter_name
functions.description: Returns the name (including :, @, $, or ?NNN) of the N-th parameter or NULL if nameless or out of range. UTF-8.
requirements: 1<=N<=count.
Do not free returned pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_parameter_index
functions.description: Returns the 1-based index of the named parameter or 0 if not found. Name must be UTF-8 and match exactly (including prefix).
requirements: zName must be NUL-terminated UTF-8.
Index 0 means not found.

functions.name: sqlite3_clear_bindings
functions.description: Resets all bound parameters in the statement to NULL. Returns SQLITE_OK.
requirements: Valid prepared statement pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_function
functions.signature: int sqlite3_create_function(sqlite3 *db, const char *zFunctionName, int nArg, int eTextRep, void *pApp, void (*xFunc)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xStep)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xFinal)(sqlite3_context*));
functions.description: Registers or redefines a SQL scalar or aggregate function on a connection using a UTF-8 name. xFunc is for scalar, xStep/xFinal for aggregate. nArg is number of args (or -1 for variable). eTextRep encodes preferred text encoding and flags (e.g., SQLITE_UTF8 | SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC).
requirements: db must be a valid open sqlite3*.
zFunctionName must be a non-NULL UTF-8 string with length ≤ 255 bytes.
If defining scalar, xFunc must be non-NULL and xStep/xFinal NULL; for aggregate, xStep/xFinal non-NULL and xFunc NULL.
nArg must be -1 or in [0,127].
eTextRep must be one of SQLITE_UTF8/16 flags optionally OR’ed with SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC/SQLITE_DIRECTONLY/SQLITE_INNOCUOUS/SQLITE_SUBTYPE/SQLITE_RESULT_SUBTYPE/SQLITE_SELFORDER1.
Thread-safety: define functions before executing statements that use them.
Do not close/finalize the db/statement from inside callbacks.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_function16
functions.signature: int sqlite3_create_function16(sqlite3 *db, const void *zFunctionName, int nArg, int eTextRep, void *pApp, void (*xFunc)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xStep)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xFinal)(sqlite3_context*));
functions.description: Same as sqlite3_create_function() but the function name is a UTF-16 string in native byte order.
requirements: zFunctionName must be a valid zero-terminated UTF-16 string in native byte order.
All other requirements are the same as sqlite3_create_function().

functions.name: sqlite3_create_function_v2
functions.signature: int sqlite3_create_function_v2(sqlite3 *db, const char *zFunctionName, int nArg, int eTextRep, void *pApp, void (*xFunc)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xStep)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xFinal)(sqlite3_context*), void(*xDestroy)(void*));
functions.description: Registers a SQL function like sqlite3_create_function(), with an additional xDestroy callback invoked to clean up pApp when the function is deleted or redefined.
requirements: Same requirements as sqlite3_create_function().
xDestroy, if not NULL, is called once when the function is deleted or redefined or if registration fails.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_window_function
functions.signature: int sqlite3_create_window_function(sqlite3 *db, const char *zFunctionName, int nArg, int eTextRep, void *pApp, void (*xStep)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xFinal)(sqlite3_context*), void (*xValue)(sqlite3_context*), void (*xInverse)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void(*xDestroy)(void*));
functions.description: Registers or redefines a SQL aggregate window function with step, final, value, and inverse callbacks.
requirements: db must be open; zFunctionName UTF-8 ≤ 255 bytes.
nArg in [0,127] or -1.
xStep and xFinal must be non-NULL; xValue/xInverse may be NULL to indicate ordinary aggregate.
eTextRep/flags as for create_function.
xDestroy called to free pApp when deregistered or on failure.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_collation
functions.signature: int sqlite3_create_collation(sqlite3*, const char *zName, int eTextRep, void *pArg, int(*xCompare)(void*,int,const void*,int,const void*));
functions.description: Registers or deletes a collation sequence with UTF-8 name zName and comparator xCompare for eTextRep encoding. If xCompare is NULL, deletes the collation.
requirements: zName must be a unique collation name (case-insensitive compare).
eTextRep must be SQLITE_UTF8/SQLITE_UTF16*/SQLITE_UTF16_ALIGNED.
xCompare must obey strict ordering properties and be deterministic.
If deleting, pass xCompare=NULL.
Do not change pArg/xCompare while in use by running statements.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_collation_v2
functions.signature: int sqlite3_create_collation_v2(sqlite3*, const char *zName, int eTextRep, void *pArg, int(*xCompare)(void*,int,const void*,int,const void*), void(*xDestroy)(void*));
functions.description: Like sqlite3_create_collation() but with xDestroy destructor for pArg when the collation is deleted or replaced or if registration fails.
requirements: Same as sqlite3_create_collation().
xDestroy is not called if the function fails to register (special case noted by docs); caller should check return and clean up if needed.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_collation16
functions.signature: int sqlite3_create_collation16(sqlite3*, const void *zName, int eTextRep, void *pArg, int(*xCompare)(void*,int,const void*,int,const void*));
functions.description: UTF-16 version of sqlite3_create_collation().
requirements: zName is UTF-16 native byte-order.
Other requirements same as sqlite3_create_collation().

functions.name: sqlite3_collation_needed
functions.signature: int sqlite3_collation_needed(sqlite3*, void*, void(*)(void*,sqlite3*,int eTextRep,const char*));
functions.description: Registers a callback to be invoked when an undefined collation is required. Callback receives eTextRep and UTF-8 collation name.
requirements: Only one callback may be registered; subsequent calls replace previous.
Callback should register the collation via sqlite3_create_collation*.
The callback may be invoked during statement preparation.

functions.name: sqlite3_collation_needed16
functions.signature: int sqlite3_collation_needed16(sqlite3*, void*, void(*)(void*,sqlite3*,int eTextRep,const void*));
functions.description: UTF-16 version of sqlite3_collation_needed(). Callback receives UTF-16 collation name in native byte order.
requirements: Same requirements as sqlite3_collation_needed().

functions.name: sqlite3_overload_function
functions.signature: int sqlite3_overload_function(sqlite3*, const char *zFuncName, int nArg);
functions.description: Ensures a global placeholder function exists for name/arity so that virtual tables can overload it via xFindFunction().
requirements: db must be open.
Registers a stub function that throws an exception when used unless overloaded.
nArg is the number of arguments for dispatch.

functions.name: sqlite3_aggregate_context
functions.description: Allocates or retrieves per-aggregate-call state for user-defined aggregate or window functions. Returns a zeroed buffer on first call, same buffer thereafter. Returns NULL if nBytes<=0 or OOM.
requirements: Must be called only from within xStep/xFinal/xInverse/xValue callbacks.
If first call uses N>0, size is fixed for the aggregate instance.
Not threadsafe across contexts; use only within the same callback context.

functions.name: sqlite3_aggregate_context
functions.description: Allocates (on first call) and returns a per-aggregate function state buffer for the current aggregate invocation. Subsequent calls return the same buffer.
requirements: Must be called from within an aggregate SQL function’s xStep or xFinal.
If nBytes<=0 on first call, returns NULL; otherwise returns zeroed buffer of nBytes on first successful call.
Buffer lifetime is until the aggregate query concludes; SQLite frees it automatically.
Call with nBytes=0 in xFinal to avoid unnecessary allocations.

functions.name: sqlite3_user_data
functions.description: Returns the application data pointer pApp that was registered with the SQL function.
requirements: Call only within a SQL function callback context.

functions.name: sqlite3_user_data
functions.description: Returns the pApp/user-data pointer associated with the application-defined function registered for this context.
requirements: Must be called from within an application-defined SQL function’s context.
User data is the same void* passed to sqlite3_create_function/16/v2().

functions.name: sqlite3_context_db_handle
functions.description: Returns the sqlite3* database connection associated with the current SQL function context.
requirements: Call only within a SQL function callback.

functions.name: sqlite3_context_db_handle
functions.description: Returns the sqlite3 database connection associated with the function invocation’s context.
requirements: Call inside an application-defined function context.

functions.name: sqlite3_get_auxdata
functions.description: Retrieves function-argument-scoped auxiliary data previously set via sqlite3_set_auxdata() for argument N (0-based) of the current SQL function call. Returns NULL if none.
requirements: Must be called within a SQL function callback.
N must be ≥0.
Auxdata may be discarded by SQLite at any time; code must handle NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_get_auxdata
functions.description: Retrieves auxiliary data previously associated with argument N of the current SQL function call via sqlite3_set_auxdata(). Useful for caching expensive computation per constant argument.
requirements: Must be called within an application-defined SQL function.
N is zero-based index for the function argument.
Returns NULL if none set or it was discarded (e.g., replan, OOM, etc.).

functions.name: sqlite3_set_auxdata
functions.signature: void sqlite3_set_auxdata(sqlite3_context*, int N, void*, void (*xDelete)(void*));
functions.description: Associates pointer data with argument N for the duration of a function instance to cache expensive computations across invocations. xDelete is called once when auxdata is discarded.
requirements: Must be called within a SQL function callback.
N must be ≥0.
xDelete may be invoked immediately (e.g., OOM) or later; auxdata may be dropped by SQLite unpredictably (e.g., during planning).

functions.name: sqlite3_set_auxdata
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_set_auxdata(sqlite3_context*, int N, void*, void (*xDelete)(void*));
functions.description: Associates a pointer with argument N of the current SQL function so it can be retrieved by sqlite3_get_auxdata() for subsequent invocations during the same statement execution. Destructor xDelete is called exactly once when SQLite discards the data.
requirements: Must be called within an application-defined SQL function.
N is zero-based index for the function argument.
If xDelete is not NULL it will be called exactly once when auxdata is discarded (may be immediately on OOM or planning).
Do not use P after calling sqlite3_set_auxdata(), since xDelete may run immediately on error.

functions.name: sqlite3_get_clientdata
functions.description: Retrieves a named client data pointer previously registered on a database connection using sqlite3_set_clientdata().
requirements: Provide the same name string used to set the client data (strcmp compared, case-sensitive).
Returns NULL if none set.
Available since 3.44.0.

functions.name: sqlite3_set_clientdata
functions.signature: int sqlite3_set_clientdata(sqlite3*, const char*, void*, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Associates a named pointer with a database connection for wrapper libraries. Optionally provides a destructor invoked when replaced, OOM during registration, or on connection close.
requirements: Name must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string; names compared using strcmp(), case-sensitive.
If both P and destructor X are non-NULL, X(P) will be called on replacement, on OOM during registration, or when the database connection closes.
Returns SQLITE_OK on success, SQLITE_NOMEM on allocation failure.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_blob
functions.signature: void sqlite3_result_blob(sqlite3_context*, const void*, int, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Sets the result of a SQL function callback to a BLOB of length N bytes. The destructor controls lifetime (SQLITE_STATIC, SQLITE_TRANSIENT, or custom).
requirements: Invoke only within a SQL function callback.
Destructor rules: SQLITE_STATIC means content valid for duration; SQLITE_TRANSIENT means copy is made; custom xDel called when SQLite is done.
If N<0, behavior undefined.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_blob64
functions.signature: void sqlite3_result_blob64(sqlite3_context*, const void*, sqlite3_uint64, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Sets the result to a BLOB of 64-bit length.
requirements: Same as sqlite3_result_blob(); length is sqlite3_uint64.
Large sizes are subject to SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH and SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_double
functions.description: Sets the result of a SQL function callback to a floating-point value.
requirements: Only valid inside SQL function callback.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_error
functions.description: Causes the SQL function to throw an error with the specified message (UTF-8). If third argument is negative, message is taken up to first NUL; otherwise exact length in bytes. SQLite makes a private copy.
requirements: Only within SQL function callback.
After calling, the function’s return is error; do not also set a result.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_error16
functions.description: Same as sqlite3_result_error() but message is UTF-16 (native byte order).
requirements: Only within SQL function callback.
See byte-order and BOM handling allowances.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_error_toobig
functions.description: Returns an error indicating a value is too large (e.g., string/blob exceeds limits).
requirements: Use within SQL function callback to signal SQLITE_TOOBIG.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_error_nomem
functions.description: Returns an out-of-memory error from a SQL function.
requirements: Use within SQL function callback to signal OOM.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_error_code
functions.description: Sets the error code for a SQL function error. Usually used with sqlite3_result_error*().
requirements: Call within SQL function callback.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_int
functions.description: Sets the result to a 32-bit integer.
requirements: Only within SQL function callback.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_int64
functions.description: Sets the result to a 64-bit integer.
requirements: Only within SQL function callback.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_null
functions.description: Sets the result to SQL NULL.
requirements: Only within SQL function callback.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text
functions.signature: void sqlite3_result_text(sqlite3_context*, const char*, int, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Sets the result to UTF-8 text of byte length N (or if N<0, up to first NUL). Destructor controls lifetime.
requirements: Only within SQL function callback.
If N≥0, it must be the byte offset where NUL would occur if NUL-terminated; embedded NULs are retained.
Destructor semantics as per blob.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text64
functions.signature: void sqlite3_result_text64(sqlite3_context*, const char*, sqlite3_uint64, void(*)(void*), unsigned char encoding);
functions.description: Sets the result to a text string of 64-bit length with specified encoding (SQLITE_UTF8/UTF16/UTF16BE/UTF16LE).
requirements: encoding must be one of SQLITE_UTF8/SQLITE_UTF16/SQLITE_UTF16BE/SQLITE_UTF16LE.
Destructor semantics as per blob.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text16
functions.signature: void sqlite3_result_text16(sqlite3_context*, const void*, int, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Sets the result to UTF-16 (native) text. If N<0, uses up to first NUL, with BOM handling.
requirements: Only within SQL function callback.
UTF-16 BOM handling as documented; may convert invalid code points to U+FFFD.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text16le
functions.signature: void sqlite3_result_text16le(sqlite3_context*, const void*, int, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Sets the result to UTF-16 little-endian text.
requirements: Only within SQL function callback.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text16be
functions.signature: void sqlite3_result_text16be(sqlite3_context*, const void*, int, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Sets the result to UTF-16 big-endian text.
requirements: Only within SQL function callback.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_value
functions.description: Sets the result to a copy of the supplied sqlite3_value (protected or unprotected). SQLite makes its own copy, so the input may be modified/freed afterward.
requirements: Only within SQL function callback.
Passing an unprotected value from sqlite3_column_value() is allowed; only use it with result_value/bind_value/value_dup.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_pointer
functions.signature: void sqlite3_result_pointer(sqlite3_context*, void*, const char*, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Sets the result to a NULL with an associated typed pointer retrievable via sqlite3_value_pointer(). For advanced pointer passing.
requirements: Only within SQL function callback.
Type string should be static (ideally a string literal).
xDestroy called when SQLite is finished with the pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_zeroblob
functions.description: Sets the result to a zero-filled BLOB of n bytes.
requirements: Only within SQL function callback.
n must be ≥0 and within configured limits.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_zeroblob64
functions.description: Sets the result to a zero-filled BLOB of n bytes (64-bit). Returns SQLITE_OK on success or error code on failure.
requirements: Only within SQL function callback.
n must not exceed configured maximum lengths.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_subtype
functions.description: Associates an 8-bit subtype with the current function result for use by downstream functions using sqlite3_value_subtype().
requirements: Call only after setting a result within the same callback.
Functions using subtypes should be registered with SQLITE_RESULT_SUBTYPE flag; strict builds may enforce this.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_subtype
functions.description: Sets the subtype on the SQL result produced by the current application-defined function context. Use to tag results so downstream functions can inspect subtype with sqlite3_value_subtype().
requirements: Must be called within an application-defined SQL function’s xFunc/xStep/xFinal context (valid sqlite3_context*).
Only lower 8 bits of subtype are currently preserved; higher bits may be discarded.
For reliable behavior on all builds, register the function with SQLITE_RESULT_SUBTYPE property; some builds may enforce this.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_subtype
functions.description: Duplicate entry for sqlite3_result_subtype; see prior entry.
requirements: Same as previous entry.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_blob
functions.description: Returns pointer to BLOB bytes for a value; may be NULL for zero-length BLOBs.
requirements: Use only with protected sqlite3_value objects (e.g., in SQL function callbacks) or with unprotected only as input to result/bind.
If conversion is needed, may allocate; check for OOM by sqlite3_errcode().

functions.name: sqlite3_value_double
functions.description: Returns floating-point value, with type conversion if necessary.
requirements: Protected sqlite3_value recommended outside of result/bind pathways.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_int
functions.description: Returns 32-bit integer value.
requirements: Protected sqlite3_value recommended outside of result/bind pathways.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_int64
functions.description: Returns 64-bit integer value.
requirements: Protected sqlite3_value recommended outside of result/bind pathways.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_pointer
functions.description: Retrieves a typed pointer previously set via sqlite3_result_pointer() or sqlite3_bind_pointer(). Returns NULL if the type string does not match.
requirements: Type string must match exactly (strcmp) the one used when setting pointer.
Protected sqlite3_value recommended.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_text
functions.description: Returns UTF-8 text for the value (zero-terminated).
requirements: May allocate for conversion; check for OOM with sqlite3_errcode().
Protected sqlite3_value recommended.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_text16
functions.description: Returns UTF-16 (native) text.
requirements: Protected sqlite3_value recommended.
May convert/allocate; check for OOM.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_text16le
functions.description: Returns UTF-16 little-endian text.
requirements: Protected sqlite3_value recommended.
May convert/allocate; check for OOM.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_text16be
functions.description: Returns UTF-16 big-endian text.
requirements: Protected sqlite3_value recommended.
May convert/allocate; check for OOM.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_bytes
functions.description: Returns number of bytes in the value when interpreted as BLOB or UTF-8 text (without NUL terminator).
requirements: If conversion is needed (numeric to text), counts bytes of converted representation.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_bytes16
functions.description: Returns number of bytes for UTF-16 encoding of the value (without NUL terminator).
requirements: May cause conversion; counts bytes, not characters.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_type
functions.description: Returns the SQLite fundamental datatype code of the value before implicit type conversions (INTEGER, FLOAT, TEXT, BLOB, NULL).
requirements: Meaningful only prior to conversion; post-conversion result is undefined though harmless.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_numeric_type
functions.description: Applies numeric affinity to the value and returns the resulting fundamental type.
requirements: May modify internal representation; use in function code that wants numeric coercion.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_nochange
functions.description: Within virtual table xUpdate(), returns non-zero if the column value indicates the column is unchanged by the UPDATE (paired with sqlite3_vtab_nochange()/sqlite3_vtab_nochange in xColumn).
requirements: Meaningful only within a virtual table xUpdate() call for an UPDATE statement.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_frombind
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the sqlite3_value originated from a bound parameter, zero if from a literal, column, or expression.
requirements: Use within SQL function callbacks or vtab methods to adjust behavior based on source.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_encoding
functions.description: Reports internal text encoding of a TEXT sqlite3_value (SQLITE_UTF8/UTF16BE/UTF16LE). For non-TEXT values the result is meaningless.
requirements: Intended for testing/validation; ordinary apps should not depend on encoding.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_subtype
functions.description: Returns application-defined subtype associated with the value (0-255). Used with sqlite3_result_subtype().
requirements: Functions that inspect subtypes should be registered with SQLITE_SUBTYPE.
May return 0 if subtype not preserved due to optimizations.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_dup
functions.description: Creates a protected copy of a sqlite3_value. Returns NULL on OOM or if input is NULL.
requirements: The returned value must be freed using sqlite3_value_free().
If the input is a pointer value (sqlite3_result_pointer/bind_pointer), the result is NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_free
functions.description: Frees a sqlite3_value previously obtained from sqlite3_value_dup().
requirements: Safe to pass NULL (no-op).
Do not free sqlite3_value objects not created by sqlite3_value_dup().

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_alloc
functions.description: Allocates a mutex object. The argument is one of SQLITE_MUTEX_FAST, SQLITE_MUTEX_RECURSIVE, or a SQLITE_MUTEX_STATIC_* selector for static mutexes.
requirements: For dynamic mutex types (FAST, RECURSIVE), returns a new mutex each call; must be freed with sqlite3_mutex_free().
For static types, returns a pointer to a static mutex; do not free.
May return NULL if unable to allocate.
Use only after sqlite3_initialize().

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_free
functions.description: Frees a dynamic mutex allocated by sqlite3_mutex_alloc(). Undefined behavior if used on a static mutex.
requirements: Argument may be NULL (no-op).
Must not be called on static mutexes.
Caller must ensure no thread holds the mutex when freeing.

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_enter
functions.description: Enters (locks) a mutex, blocking if necessary. Recursive if the mutex is recursive.
requirements: Argument may be NULL (no-op).
Do not attempt to recursively enter a non-recursive mutex.
Must be paired with sqlite3_mutex_leave().

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_try
functions.description: Attempts to enter a mutex without blocking. Returns SQLITE_OK on success or SQLITE_BUSY if it cannot be acquired immediately.
requirements: Argument may be NULL (treated as success).
Some platforms may always return SQLITE_BUSY for try; SQLite core tolerates this except in certain builds needing try.

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_leave
functions.description: Leaves (unlocks) a previously entered mutex.
requirements: Argument may be NULL (no-op).
Undefined behavior if called by a thread that does not hold the mutex.

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_held
functions.description: Debug helper that returns true if the mutex is currently held by the calling thread. Used only in assert builds; may be stubbed to always return true.
requirements: If argument is NULL, must return 1.
Used for assertions; not for general program logic.

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_notheld
functions.description: Debug helper that returns true if the mutex is not held by the calling thread. Only in assert builds; may be stubbed.
requirements: If argument is NULL, must return 1.
Used for assertions; not for general program logic.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_mutex
functions.description: Returns the database connection mutex when in serialized mode; NULL in multi-thread or single-thread modes.
requirements: db must be a valid open sqlite3*.
Only meaningful if threading mode is Serialized.

functions.name: sqlite3_file_control
functions.signature: int sqlite3_file_control(sqlite3*, const char *zDbName, int op, void*);
functions.description: Sends a control opcode to the VFS for the specified schema ("main", "temp", or attached db name). Some opcodes are handled by core (e.g., FILE_POINTER, JOURNAL_POINTER, VFS_POINTER, DATA_VERSION). Returns SQLITE_OK on success or an error code.
requirements: zDbName must be the exact schema name or NULL for "main".
For unknown zDbName, returns SQLITE_ERROR (not stored in db errcode).
The pArg must point to the appropriate type for the given opcode.
VFS may return SQLITE_NOTFOUND for unrecognized opcodes.

functions.name: sqlite3_test_control
functions.description: Internal/testing interface to inject faults and read internal state. Not for application use. Behavior may change without notice.
requirements: Do not use in production applications.
Correct argument types must be supplied per op, otherwise undefined behavior.

functions.name: sqlite3_status
functions.signature: int sqlite3_status(int op, int *pCurrent, int *pHighwater, int resetFlag);
functions.description: Reports global library status metrics (memory usage, pagecache usage, etc.). Writes current and high-water values; may reset high-water if resetFlag is true. Returns SQLITE_OK.
requirements: op must be a valid SQLITE_STATUS_* code.
If pCurrent or pHighwater is NULL, that field is not written.
Values may be truncated to 32-bit; use sqlite3_status64() for large values.

functions.name: sqlite3_status64
