functions.signature: int sqlite3_status64(int op, sqlite3_int64 *pCurrent, sqlite3_int64 *pHighwater, int resetFlag);
functions.description: 64-bit version of sqlite3_status().
requirements: Same as sqlite3_status() with 64-bit outputs.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_status
functions.signature: int sqlite3_db_status(sqlite3*, int op, int *pCur, int *pHiwtr, int resetFlg);
functions.description: Reports per-connection status counters (lookaside, cache used, schema used, statement memory, cache hit/miss, etc.). Returns SQLITE_OK.
requirements: op must be a valid SQLITE_DBSTATUS_* code.
resetFlg resets highwater where applicable.
Some counters only have current or only have high-water values.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_status64
functions.signature: int sqlite3_db_status64(sqlite3*, int op, sqlite3_int64 *pCur, sqlite3_int64 *pHiwtr, int resetFlg);
functions.description: 64-bit version of sqlite3_db_status().
requirements: Same as sqlite3_db_status(), with 64-bit outputs.

functions.name: sqlite3_stmt_status
functions.signature: int sqlite3_stmt_status(sqlite3_stmt*, int op, int resetFlg);
functions.description: Returns performance counters for a prepared statement (fullscan steps, sorts, autoindex, VM steps, reprpares, runs, filter hits/misses, memused). If resetFlg is non-zero, the counter is reset after read.
requirements: op must be one of SQLITE_STMTSTATUS_* codes.
Only certain counters are meaningful; some are approximations.

functions.name: sqlite3_backup_init
functions.signature: sqlite3_backup *sqlite3_backup_init(sqlite3 *pDest, const char *zDestName, sqlite3 *pSource, const char *zSourceName);
functions.description: Begins an online backup from source schema to destination schema. Returns an sqlite3_backup* handle or NULL and sets an error on pDest.
requirements: pDest and pSource must be different connections.
zDestName/zSourceName must be schema names (e.g., "main", "temp").
Fails if a read or read-write txn is open on destination.
Handle must be finalized with sqlite3_backup_finish().

functions.name: sqlite3_backup_step
functions.description: Copies up to nPage pages from source to destination. Returns SQLITE_OK while more pages remain, SQLITE_DONE when complete, or error codes (READONLY, NOMEM, BUSY, LOCKED, IOERR_XXX).
requirements: p must be a valid backup handle.
If nPage<0, copies all remaining pages.
May require busy-handler cooperation; BUSY/LOCKED indicate retry later.
Do not call after finish().

functions.name: sqlite3_backup_finish
functions.description: Releases backup resources and commits or rolls back the destination transaction appropriately. Returns SQLITE_OK if no errors occurred; otherwise last error.
requirements: Must be called exactly once for each successful backup_init().
Safe to call even if step() errors occurred; returns error code.

functions.name: sqlite3_backup_remaining
functions.description: Returns number of pages remaining to be backed up.
requirements: Valid only for an active backup handle.
May return 0 after completion.

functions.name: sqlite3_backup_pagecount
functions.description: Returns total page count in the source database.
requirements: Valid only for an active backup handle.

functions.name: sqlite3_enable_shared_cache
functions.description: Globally enables or disables shared page-cache mode for the process. Discouraged. Returns SQLITE_OK or an error code.
requirements: Should not be used; prefer per-connection flags.
Threadsafe only on platforms where 32-bit writes are atomic.
Disabled on certain platforms (always returns SQLITE_MISUSE on macOS/iOS as documented).

functions.name: sqlite3_release_memory
functions.description: Attempts to free N bytes from non-essential internal caches (e.g., page cache). Returns number of bytes actually freed. No-op if memory management disabled.
requirements: Advisory; may free less or more than requested.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_release_memory
functions.description: Attempts to free as much heap memory as possible from the specified connection’s caches.
requirements: db must be open; returns SQLITE_OK regardless, or error on failure.

functions.name: sqlite3_soft_heap_limit
functions.description: Deprecated. Use sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64(). Sets a soft limit on heap allocations for all connections.
requirements: Advisory only; SQLite strives to stay below the limit.
Prefer sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64().

functions.name: sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64
functions.description: Sets or queries the global soft heap limit. Returns prior limit (or negative on error).
requirements: N<0 queries without changes.
0 disables soft limit.
Soft limit cannot exceed hard limit if set.

functions.name: sqlite3_hard_heap_limit64
functions.description: Sets a hard upper bound on total heap memory used by SQLite. Returns prior hard limit (or negative on error).
requirements: N<0 queries without changes.
0 disables hard limit.
Soft limit auto-adjusted if needed to be ≤ hard limit.

functions.name: sqlite3_table_column_metadata
functions.signature: int sqlite3_table_column_metadata(sqlite3 *db, const char *zDbName, const char *zTableName, const char *zColumnName, char const **pzDataType, char const **pzCollSeq, int *pNotNull, int *pPrimaryKey, int *pAutoinc);
functions.description: Retrieves metadata for a named column of a table: declared type, default collation, NOT NULL, primary key, autoincrement flags.
requirements: db must be open; zDbName may be NULL to search all schemas.
If zColumnName is NULL, it checks table existence.
Fails with SQLITE_ERROR if the column or table does not exist or table is a view.
Returned strings are managed by SQLite; valid until schema changes.

functions.name: sqlite3_load_extension
functions.signature: int sqlite3_load_extension(sqlite3 *db, const char *zFile, const char *zProc, char **pzErrMsg);
functions.description: Loads a shared library as an SQLite extension and invokes its entry point. Requires load extension to be enabled. Returns SQLITE_OK or SQLITE_ERROR with *pzErrMsg set.
requirements: Load extension must be enabled via sqlite3_enable_load_extension() or SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION C-API.
zFile is library path; zProc may be NULL (defaults to sqlite3_extension_init or derived name).
Caller must free *pzErrMsg with sqlite3_free() on error.
Security: Prefer enabling only C-API; keep SQL load_extension() disabled.

functions.name: sqlite3_enable_load_extension
functions.description: Enables or disables both the C-API sqlite3_load_extension() and SQL load_extension() functions on a connection. Returns SQLITE_OK.
requirements: Security: Recommended to use SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION instead to keep SQL function disabled.
onoff==1 enables; 0 disables.

functions.name: sqlite3_auto_extension
functions.description: Registers a statically linked extension entry point to be invoked for each new database connection. Returns SQLITE_OK.
requirements: xEntryPoint must have prototype int x(sqlite3*, char**, const sqlite3_api_routines*), although declared void(*)(void).
No-op if entry point already registered.
Must be safe to call during sqlite3_open(); do not close/finalize within.

functions.name: sqlite3_cancel_auto_extension
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered automatic extension entry point. Returns 1 if unregistered, 0 if not found.
requirements: xEntryPoint must match exactly the function pointer registered earlier.

functions.name: sqlite3_reset_auto_extension
functions.description: Unregisters all automatically loaded extensions.
requirements: Affects process-global state.

functions.name: sqlite3_sleep
functions.description: Suspends the current thread for at least the specified milliseconds. Returns milliseconds requested of the OS.
requirements: Negative values are coerced to zero before passing to VFS.
Actual sleep precision depends on platform.
Implemented via VFS xSleep.

functions.name: sqlite3_temp_directory
functions.description: Global pointer to override the directory used for temporary files by built-in VFSes. Discouraged for new applications.
requirements: If modified directly, set to memory allocated by sqlite3_malloc() or NULL.
Not thread-safe to read/write concurrently.
May be modified by PRAGMA temp_store_directory (manages memory).
Set once during process init for safety.

functions.name: sqlite3_data_directory
functions.description: Windows-specific: global pointer to override the default base directory for relative database paths. Ignored on unix VFSes.
requirements: Changing it while connections are open can corrupt databases.
Not thread-safe to read/write concurrently.
May be modified by PRAGMA data_store_directory (manages memory).
Set once during process init for safety.

functions.name: sqlite3_win32_set_directory
functions.description: Windows-only: Sets sqlite3_temp_directory or sqlite3_data_directory depending on type. Returns SQLITE_OK, SQLITE_ERROR for unsupported type, SQLITE_NOMEM on allocation failure.
requirements: type must be SQLITE_WIN32_DATA_DIRECTORY_TYPE or SQLITE_WIN32_TEMP_DIRECTORY_TYPE.
zValue points to UTF-8 or UTF-16 depending on the specific function variant (this generic uses void*; prefer 8/16 variants).
Passing NULL frees previous value (via sqlite3_free()) and clears.

functions.name: sqlite3_win32_set_directory8
functions.signature: int sqlite3_win32_set_directory8(unsigned long type, const char *zValue);
functions.description: Windows-only: UTF-8 version of sqlite3_win32_set_directory().
requirements: See sqlite3_win32_set_directory().

functions.name: sqlite3_win32_set_directory16
functions.signature: int sqlite3_win32_set_directory16(unsigned long type, const void *zValue);
functions.description: Windows-only: UTF-16 version of sqlite3_win32_set_directory().
requirements: See sqlite3_win32_set_directory().

functions.name: sqlite3_get_autocommit
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the connection is currently in autocommit mode, zero otherwise. Autocommit is on by default and toggles via BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK.
requirements: db must be valid and open.
Use for determining if a transaction is active.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_handle
functions.description: Returns the database connection associated with a prepared statement.
requirements: pStmt must be a valid prepared statement pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_name
functions.description: Returns the schema name for the N-th database on the connection (0="main", 1="temp", higher for ATTACHed). May be invalidated by schema-changing operations.
requirements: db must be open; N must be within range or NULL is returned.
Copy the returned string if it needs to be kept beyond potential schema changes or across threads.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_filename
functions.description: Returns the absolute filename used by schema zDbName (e.g., "main","temp" or attached name) for database connection db, or NULL/empty string for in-memory/temp.
requirements: zDbName must be the schema name.
Returned string is owned by SQLite; valid until db detaches/closes or schema changes; copy if needed beyond.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_readonly
functions.description: Returns 1 if schema zDbName on db is read-only, 0 if read/write, or -1 if zDbName is not a known database on db.
requirements: zDbName must name an attached database.

functions.name: sqlite3_txn_state
functions.description: Reports transaction state for schema zSchema on connection: SQLITE_TXN_NONE (0), _READ (1), or _WRITE (2). If zSchema is NULL, returns highest state across schemas. Returns -1 if invalid schema name.
requirements: zSchema should be NULL or a valid schema name (e.g., "main","temp", or attached).

functions.name: sqlite3_next_stmt
functions.description: Iterates prepared statements on a connection. Pass pStmt=NULL to get first; then pass previous to get next; returns NULL when done.
requirements: pDb must be an open sqlite3*.
Do not finalize pStmt between calls unless you intend to stop iterating that stmt.

functions.name: sqlite3_commit_hook
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked when a transaction is committed. If callback returns non-zero, SQLite rolls back the transaction. Returns the previous pArg of the last registered hook or NULL.
requirements: Only one commit hook per connection; new overrides previous.
Callback must not modify the invoking db connection (including preparing/stepping statements).
Return 0 to allow commit, non-zero to force rollback.

functions.name: sqlite3_rollback_hook
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked when a transaction is rolled back. Returns previous pArg or NULL.
requirements: Only one rollback hook per connection; new overrides previous.
Callback must not modify the invoking db connection.

functions.name: sqlite3_autovacuum_pages
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_autovacuum_pages(sqlite3 *db, unsigned int(*xCallback)(void*,const char*,unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int), void *pArg, void(*xDelete)(void*));
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked during autovacuum to decide how many free pages to remove. The callback can tune compaction amount per database file.
requirements: xCallback should be thread-safe and must not call into SQLite APIs; not reentrant.
Return number of free pages to remove; 0 to skip; >= free pages for full.
One callback per connection; subsequent calls override and may free prior pArg via xDelete.
Returns SQLITE_OK or SQLITE_MISUSE.

functions.name: sqlite3_update_hook
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void *sqlite3_update_hook(sqlite3*, void(*)(void *,int ,char const*,char const*,sqlite3_int64), void*);
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked on row changes (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) on rowid tables. Reports db name, table name, operation code, and rowid.
requirements: Only one update hook per connection; overriding replaces prior.
Not invoked for WITHOUT ROWID tables or internal system tables.
Callback must not modify the invoking db connection.

functions.name: sqlite3_wal_hook
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked after a WAL commit (or in place of xSync if synchronous=OFF). Reports schema name and number of pages in WAL. Return value is ignored (should return SQLITE_OK).
requirements: Only one WAL hook per connection; overriding replaces prior.
Callback must be fast, not reentrant, and avoid calling SQLite APIs that could reenter the same connection.

functions.name: sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint
functions.description: Configures automatic checkpoints: when WAL has N or more frames, SQLite checkpoints. Pass <=0 to disable. Returns SQLITE_OK or error.
requirements: Affects the connection db; overwrites any WAL hook set by sqlite3_wal_hook via internal use.
Use WAL mode databases only.

functions.name: sqlite3_wal_checkpoint
functions.description: Runs a passive checkpoint on database zDb (or all if NULL/empty). Equivalent to sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2(..., SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE, NULL, NULL).
requirements: db must be open; zDb is schema name or NULL.
Returns SQLite error codes; does not set *pnLog/*pnCkpt.

functions.name: sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2(sqlite3 *db, const char *zDb, int eMode, int *pnLog, int *pnCkpt);
functions.description: Runs a WAL checkpoint in mode eMode (NOOP, PASSIVE, FULL, RESTART, TRUNCATE). Optionally returns WAL frame count and frames checkpointed.
requirements: zDb is schema or NULL for all attached DBs.
May block and invoke busy-handler for FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE; PASSIVE never blocks writers.
pnLog/pnCkpt may be NULL. When zDb NULL, their values are undefined.
Returns SQLITE_BUSY if another checkpoint running, or appropriate errors.

functions.name: sqlite3_vfs_find
functions.description: Finds a registered VFS by name, or returns the default VFS if zVfsName is NULL. Returns NULL if not found.
requirements: zVfsName is case-sensitive name or NULL.
Use only to inspect or chain VFSes.

functions.name: sqlite3_vfs_register
functions.description: Registers a VFS. If makeDflt is non-zero, also makes it the process default VFS.
requirements: pVfs->iVersion and methods must be properly filled.
Do not register two VFSes with same name.

functions.name: sqlite3_vfs_unregister
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered VFS. If it was default, another arbitrary VFS becomes default.
requirements: pVfs must have been registered.
No open connections should be using it.

functions.name: sqlite3_blob_open
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_blob_open(sqlite3 *db, const char *zDb, const char *zTable, const char *zColumn, sqlite3_int64 iRow, int flags, sqlite3_blob **ppBlob);
functions.description: Opens a handle for incremental BLOB I/O on zDb.zTable.zColumn at row iRow. If flags!=0, opens read-write; else read-only.
requirements: zDb is schema name ("main","temp", or attached).
zTable must exist and not be WITHOUT ROWID; zColumn must be a TEXT or BLOB column; iRow must exist (or SQLITE_ERROR).
Read-write fails if column is PK/UNIQUE or child key under FK, or DB/column is read-only.
ppBlob is set to NULL on failure except SQLITE_MISUSE.
Close with sqlite3_blob_close().

functions.name: sqlite3_blob_reopen
functions.description: Moves an existing blob handle to refer to row iRow of the same table/column. More efficient than closing and reopening.
requirements: pBlob must be open; column/table/schema unchanged.
May fail with SQLITE_ERROR and leave handle aborted (future ops return SQLITE_ABORT) if row missing or invalid type.

functions.name: sqlite3_blob_bytes
functions.description: Returns size in bytes of the blob referenced by pBlob.
requirements: pBlob must be a valid open blob handle.

functions.name: sqlite3_blob_read
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_blob_read(sqlite3_blob *pBlob, void *Z, int N, int iOffset);
functions.description: Reads N bytes from blob at offset iOffset into buffer Z.
requirements: pBlob must be open; N>=0; iOffset>=0 and iOffset+N<=blob size else SQLITE_ERROR and no read.
Returns SQLITE_ABORT if handle expired; buffer Z must be large enough.

functions.name: sqlite3_blob_write
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_blob_write(sqlite3_blob *pBlob, const void *z, int n, int iOffset);
functions.description: Writes n bytes from buffer z to blob at offset iOffset. Only for read-write handles.
requirements: Handle must be opened read-write; writing beyond blob size is not allowed (returns SQLITE_ERROR).
n>=0; iOffset>=0; returns SQLITE_ABORT if expired; may return SQLITE_READONLY/CONSTRAINT errors.
Does not change blob size.

functions.name: sqlite3_blob_close
functions.description: Closes and frees a blob handle. If it was the last read-write handle and autocommit is on, commit is attempted; error returns rollback and code.
requirements: Safe to call with NULL (no-op).
After close, do not use pBlob.

functions.name: sqlite3_vtab_config
functions.description: Called from a virtual table’s xCreate/xConnect to set interface options such as SQLITE_VTAB_CONSTRAINT_SUPPORT, SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS, SQLITE_VTAB_DIRECTONLY, or SQLITE_VTAB_USES_ALL_SCHEMAS.
requirements: Must be invoked only within xCreate or xConnect for a vtab on this db.
Pass appropriate op and any extra arguments as documented; returns SQLITE_OK or error.

functions.name: sqlite3_vtab_on_conflict
functions.description: Returns current ON CONFLICT mode for the SQL statement invoking the vtab, one of SQLITE_ROLLBACK, IGNORE, FAIL, ABORT, or REPLACE.
requirements: Must be called within a virtual table method (e.g., xUpdate) on db.

functions.name: sqlite3_declare_vtab
functions.description: In xCreate/xConnect declares the virtual table schema using a CREATE TABLE statement string zSQL.
requirements: Must be called in xCreate/xConnect for the vtab on db before returning SQLITE_OK.
zSQL must be a valid CREATE TABLE with column declarations and PK if desired.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_module
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_module(sqlite3 *db, const char *zName, const sqlite3_module *p, void *pClientData);
functions.description: Registers a virtual table module named zName with methods p and client data pClientData. Overrides existing with same name or removes if p==NULL.
requirements: db open; p points to complete module methods (or NULL to drop).
Module persists until unregistered or connection closes.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_module_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_module_v2(sqlite3 *db, const char *zName, const sqlite3_module *p, void *pClientData, void(*xDestroy)(void*));
functions.description: Like sqlite3_create_module, but calls xDestroy(pClientData) when module is replaced or db closes.
requirements: xDestroy may be NULL; will be called exactly once if registration succeeds.

functions.name: sqlite3_drop_modules
functions.description: Removes all registered modules from db except those named in azKeep (NULL-terminated array). If azKeep is NULL, removes all.
requirements: Call with azKeep as NULL or array terminated by NULL.
Affects only this db connection.

functions.name: sqlite3_vtab_rhs_value
functions.description: From within xBestIndex(), fetches the right-hand side value of constraint iCons (from aConstraint[]) if it is known. Returns SQLITE_OK and *ppVal set, or SQLITE_NOTFOUND if not available.
requirements: Must be called only from xBestIndex with the exact sqlite3_index_info* passed in.
Only available when RHS is a literal constant; ppVal is protected and valid only during xBestIndex.

functions.name: sqlite3_vtab_distinct
functions.description: From xBestIndex(), returns an integer 0..3 describing DISTINCT/ORDER BY requirements so vtab may set orderByConsumed and possibly omit duplicates as per docs.
requirements: Call only from xBestIndex with its sqlite3_index_info*.
Must set orderByConsumed only when you can satisfy constraints; else return 0..3 informative only.

functions.name: sqlite3_vtab_in
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_vtab_in(sqlite3_index_info*, int iCons, int bHandle);
functions.description: From xBestIndex(), detect and/or select all-at-once processing of an IN constraint for aConstraint[iCons]. Pass bHandle=-1 to test availability; bHandle>=0 to request (1) or decline (0) all-at-once processing.
requirements: Call only from xBestIndex; consistent results per P,N within call.
Select all-at-once only if also setting argvIndex>0 for that constraint.

functions.name: sqlite3_vtab_in_first
functions.description: Within xFilter(), iterates first value on RHS of an IN argument previously opted-in for all-at-once via sqlite3_vtab_in. Sets *ppOut to first sqlite3_value and returns SQLITE_OK; returns SQLITE_DONE and *ppOut=NULL when no values.
requirements: pVal must be the xFilter argv[argvIndex-1] for an IN opted-in all-at-once.
ppOut valid until next _in_first/_in_next call or until xFilter returns.

functions.name: sqlite3_vtab_in_next
functions.description: Continues iteration over RHS values for an IN argument begun by sqlite3_vtab_in_first(). Returns SQLITE_OK with *ppOut set, or SQLITE_DONE with *ppOut NULL at end.
requirements: Same as sqlite3_vtab_in_first() for pVal.
ppOut lifetime same as above.

functions.name: sqlite3_keyword_count
functions.description: Returns the number of SQL language keywords recognized by SQLite.

functions.name: sqlite3_keyword_name
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_keyword_name(int N, const char **pzName, int *pnName);
functions.description: Writes the N-th keyword name (UTF-8, not NUL-terminated) and byte length. Returns SQLITE_OK if N in range else SQLITE_ERROR. pzName/pnName must be valid pointers.
requirements: N must be 0..sqlite3_keyword_count()-1.
Output pointers must be non-NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_keyword_check
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_keyword_check(const char *zName, int nName);
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the given identifier (UTF-8, length nName) is a keyword; zero otherwise.
requirements: zName must point to at least nName bytes.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_new
functions.description: Creates a dynamic string builder bound to db for limits and OOM handling. Always returns a usable handle; in OOM it is a special sink that records NOMEM.
requirements: Destroy with sqlite3_str_finish().
db may be NULL; length limits default to SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_finish
functions.description: Finalizes the dynamic string and returns a malloc’d char* buffer with the built string (or NULL on OOM or empty string). Frees the sqlite3_str object.
requirements: Caller must sqlite3_free() the returned buffer.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_appendf
functions.description: Appends formatted text (printf-like) to the sqlite3_str builder.
requirements: p must be a valid sqlite3_str*.
On OOM, it becomes error-sink; further appends are ignored.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_vappendf
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_str_vappendf(sqlite3_str*, const char *zFormat, va_list);
functions.description: Varargs form of sqlite3_str_appendf().
requirements: va_list must be valid.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_append
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_str_append(sqlite3_str*, const char *zIn, int N);
functions.description: Appends exactly N bytes from zIn to the builder (or until first NUL if N<0 treated internally by caller).
requirements: zIn must point to at least N bytes if N>=0.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_appendall
functions.description: Appends entire zero-terminated string zIn to the builder.
requirements: zIn must be NUL-terminated.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_appendchar
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_str_appendchar(sqlite3_str*, int N, char C);
functions.description: Appends N copies of character C to the builder.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_reset
functions.description: Resets the sqlite3_str content to empty while preserving the error/OOM status and capacity.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_errcode
functions.description: Returns the current error code on the builder: SQLITE_OK, SQLITE_NOMEM, SQLITE_TOOBIG, etc. Once non-OK, builder stays error-sink.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_length
functions.description: Returns the current length in bytes (excluding NUL) of the builder content.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_value
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal buffer; valid until next append/reset/finish. Do not free.
requirements: Use only before finish, for inspection/reference; content changes on next append/reset.

functions.name: sqlite3_system_errno
functions.description: Attempts to return the underlying OS error code (e.g., errno on POSIX) associated with the most recent I/O/open failure on the connection.
requirements: Meaningful only immediately after an I/O/open failure like SQLITE_CANTOPEN/IOERR/etc.

functions.name: sqlite3_trace
functions.signature: SQLITE_API SQLITE_DEPRECATED void *sqlite3_trace(sqlite3*, void(*xTrace)(void*,const char*), void*);
functions.description: Deprecated tracing API. Registers a callback invoked with the SQL text as statements begin. Prefer sqlite3_trace_v2().
requirements: Only one trace callback per connection; this disables sqlite3_profile().
Function is deprecated; use sqlite3_trace_v2().

functions.name: sqlite3_trace_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_trace_v2(sqlite3*, unsigned uMask, int(*xCallback)(unsigned,void*,void*,void*), void *pCtx);
functions.description: Registers an enhanced trace callback for events indicated by uMask (SQLITE_TRACE_STMT, PROFILE, ROW, CLOSE). Callback returns int (currently ignored).
requirements: Only one trace_v2 callback per connection; overrides prior trace/profile.
xCallback must be reentrancy-safe and not call into the same db in unsafe ways.

functions.name: sqlite3_profile
functions.signature: SQLITE_API SQLITE_DEPRECATED void *sqlite3_profile(sqlite3*, void(*xProfile)(void*,const char*,sqlite3_uint64), void*);
functions.description: Deprecated profiling API; registers callback invoked with SQL text and approximate nanoseconds elapsed per statement. Cancelled by sqlite3_trace[_v2].
requirements: Only one profile callback; use trace_v2 with SQLITE_TRACE_PROFILE instead.

functions.name: sqlite3_log
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_log(int iErrCode, const char *zFormat, ...);
functions.description: Writes a formatted message to the global SQLite error log, if configured via SQLITE_CONFIG_LOG.
requirements: Not reentrant into SQLite APIs; do not call other SQLite functions from within logging callback.
zFormat must not be NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_stricmp
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_stricmp(const char *, const char *);
functions.description: Case-insensitive comparison of two UTF-8 strings using SQLite’s ASCII case-folding for identifiers. Returns 0 if equal.
requirements: Pointers must be valid C strings.

functions.name: sqlite3_strnicmp
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_strnicmp(const char *, const char *, int);
functions.description: Case-insensitive comparison of up to n bytes of two UTF-8 strings using SQLite’s ASCII case-folding. Returns 0 if equal (for first n).
requirements: n>=0; strings must be at least n bytes or NUL-terminated before.

functions.name: sqlite3_strglob
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_strglob(const char *zGlob, const char *zStr);
functions.description: GLOB pattern match: returns 0 if zStr matches zGlob pattern, non-zero otherwise. Case-sensitive.
requirements: Both pointers must be valid NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: sqlite3_strlike
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_strlike(const char *zPattern, const char *zStr, unsigned int cEsc);
functions.description: LIKE pattern match with escape character cEsc. Returns 0 if match, non-zero otherwise. Case-insensitive for ASCII.
requirements: zPattern and zStr must be valid strings; cEsc is escape char (0 means none).

functions.name: sqlite3_serialize
functions.signature: SQLITE_API unsigned char *sqlite3_serialize(sqlite3 *db, const char *zSchema, sqlite3_int64 *piSize, unsigned int mFlags);
functions.description: Returns a malloc’d buffer containing a serialization of schema zSchema (or main if NULL). If SQLITE_SERIALIZE_NOCOPY is set and contiguous memory exists (e.g., after deserialize), returns internal pointer without copying.
requirements: Caller must sqlite3_free() returned buffer unless NOCOPY path returns internal pointer—then it remains valid until next write or close.
piSize, if not NULL, receives size even if returning NULL.
May return NULL on OOM or when NOCOPY requested but no contiguous buffer exists.

functions.name: sqlite3_deserialize
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_deserialize(sqlite3 *db, const char *zSchema, unsigned char *pData, sqlite3_int64 szDb, sqlite3_int64 szBuf, unsigned mFlags);
functions.description: Replaces schema zSchema with an in-memory database from buffer pData of szDb bytes, with capacity szBuf and flags (FREEONCLOSE, RESIZEABLE, READONLY).
requirements: db must not be in autocommit mode with active tx; schema must not be TEMP; returns SQLITE_ERROR otherwise.
If FREEONCLOSE, buffer must be sqlite3_malloc memory; will be freed on close.
If RESIZEABLE, buffer may be grown via sqlite3_realloc64; implies FREEONCLOSE.
If READONLY, deserialized db is read-only.
WAL-mode files must be forced to rollback mode by setting header versions if needed.

functions.name: sqlite3_snapshot_get
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_snapshot_get(sqlite3 *db, const char *zSchema, sqlite3_snapshot **ppSnapshot);
functions.description: Takes a snapshot of the current state of WAL-mode database schema zSchema (opening a read-transaction if needed) and returns a handle recording that state.
requirements: db must not be in autocommit mode with a write tx; no write transaction open on zSchema; WAL mode; at least one transaction has been written to current WAL.
On success, caller must free with sqlite3_snapshot_free().

functions.name: sqlite3_snapshot_open
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_snapshot_open(sqlite3 *db, const char *zSchema, sqlite3_snapshot *pSnapshot);
functions.description: Starts/upgrades a read-transaction on zSchema so that it sees the historical version identified by pSnapshot.
requirements: Connection must not be in autocommit; no active statements for existing read tx; zSchema must be WAL; db must know WAL status (possibly run a harmless pragma first).
May return SQLITE_ERROR_SNAPSHOT if snapshot overwritten by checkpoint.

functions.name: sqlite3_snapshot_free
functions.description: Frees an sqlite3_snapshot obtained from sqlite3_snapshot_get().
requirements: Safe to pass NULL (no-op).

functions.name: sqlite3_snapshot_cmp
functions.description: Compares two snapshots for the same database: <0 if p1 older than p2, 0 if equal, >0 if p1 newer. Undefined if not same DB or if either predates current WAL lifecycle.
requirements: Both snapshots must have been obtained since the last WAL file reset (revert to rollback or readers->0).

functions.name: sqlite3_snapshot_recover
functions.description: Scans WAL to recover older snapshots for zDb so sqlite3_snapshot_open can use them. Only when a WAL file persists across connections.
requirements: No transaction may be open on zDb; zDb must be WAL mode.
Returns SQLITE_OK or an error.

functions.name: sqlite3_carray_bind
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_carray_bind(sqlite3_stmt *pStmt, int i, void *aData, int nData, int mFlags, void (*xDel)(void*));
functions.description: Binds a C array as argument i to the carray() table-valued function. aData points to array of nData elements of type mFlags (SQLITE_CARRAY_*). xDel, if not NULL, called on aData when no longer needed.
requirements: pStmt must have a carray(?) argument at index i.
mFlags must be one of SQLITE_CARRAY_INT32/INT64/DOUBLE/TEXT/BLOB.
xDel is invoked even on bind failure (except special SQLITE_TRANSIENT has no effect here).

functions.name: sqlite3_rtree_geometry_callback
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_rtree_geometry_callback(sqlite3 *db, const char *zGeom, int (*xGeom)(sqlite3_rtree_geometry*, int, sqlite3_rtree_dbl*, int*), void *pContext);
functions.description: Registers a geometry callback named zGeom for use in R-Tree MATCH queries. The xGeom is invoked with parameters and returns inclusion/result.
requirements: db open; used by rtree module only.
xGeom should set result and return SQLITE_OK; can use pContext for user data; may set sqlite3_rtree_geometry::pUser and xDelUser for cleanup.

functions.name: sqlite3_rtree_query_callback
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_rtree_query_callback(sqlite3 *db, const char *zQueryFunc, int (*xQueryFunc)(sqlite3_rtree_query_info*), void *pContext, void (*xDestructor)(void*));
functions.description: Registers a scored geometry query callback for R-Tree MATCH, with access to detailed query info and ability to set score and visibility.
requirements: xQueryFunc fills eWithin/rScore and may use pContext; xDestructor called on pContext when deregistered.
Return SQLITE_OK or error.

functions.name: sqlite3session_create
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3session_create(sqlite3 *db, const char *zDb, sqlite3_session **ppSession);
functions.description: Creates a session object attached to database handle db (schema zDb) to record table changes. Session uses preupdate hook; not compatible with independent preupdate hooks.
requirements: ppSession must be freed with sqlite3session_delete() before db is closed.
Cannot create session if a preupdate hook is already installed on db.

functions.name: sqlite3session_delete
functions.description: Deletes a session object and releases resources. Must be called before its db handle is closed.
requirements: After deletion, any session functions on pSession are undefined.

functions.name: sqlite3session_object_config
functions.description: Configures a session object. Supported ops: SQLITE_SESSION_OBJCONFIG_SIZE (enable/disable changeset size computation) and SQLITE_SESSION_OBJCONFIG_ROWID (enable capturing of rowid-less tables by treating implicit _rowid_).
requirements: Must be called before attaching first table; otherwise SQLITE_MISUSE.
pArg must point to int in/out per option.

functions.name: sqlite3session_enable
functions.description: Enables (>0) or disables (<=0) recording of changes. Returns final state 1(enabled) or 0(disabled).

functions.name: sqlite3session_indirect
functions.description: Sets or queries the indirect-change flag that marks subsequent changes as indirect (e.g., via triggers). Returns final state (1 or 0).

functions.name: sqlite3session_attach
functions.description: Attaches table zTab to the session for change recording. If zTab is NULL, all tables (including future ones) are tracked. Tables without PRIMARY KEY are ignored.
requirements: No error if table missing or lacks PK; changes for rows with NULL in any PK column are ignored.

functions.name: sqlite3session_table_filter
functions.description: Sets a filter callback evaluated for tables not explicitly attached. If it returns non-zero for table name, changes are recorded; zero to ignore.
requirements: Only affects tables not explicitly attached; table name is provided as zTab.

functions.name: sqlite3session_changeset
functions.description: Produces a changeset blob for all recorded changes on attached tables, compared to current database content (coalesces sequences of changes). Caller must sqlite3_free() *ppChangeset.
requirements: pSession must be valid; result size/out pointer set to 0 on error.
Memory owned by caller to free.

functions.name: sqlite3session_changeset_size
functions.description: If enabled via object_config SIZE, returns an upper bound for bytes of the next changeset output; else returns 0.
requirements: Must enable SQLITE_SESSION_OBJCONFIG_SIZE before attaching first table.

functions.name: sqlite3session_diff
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3session_diff(sqlite3_session *pSession, const char *zFromDb, const char *zTbl, char **pzErrMsg);
functions.description: Adds to the session the changes needed to transform table zTbl in database zFromDb into the current content of the attached table (same name and compatible schema).
requirements: zTbl must be or become attached to session (if not, this call attaches it).
If incompatible schemas, returns SQLITE_SCHEMA and *pzErrMsg may be set (free with sqlite3_free()).
Ignores tables without PK.

functions.name: sqlite3session_patchset
functions.description: Produces a patchset (a compact changeset omitting old values for DELETEs and UPDATEs). Caller must sqlite3_free() *ppPatchset.
requirements: Same memory/free requirements as changeset.

functions.name: sqlite3session_isempty
functions.description: Returns non-zero if session has recorded no changes (note: changeset output may still be empty even if this is zero due to net-no-op sequences).

functions.name: sqlite3session_memory_used
functions.description: Returns number of bytes of heap memory used by the session.

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_start
functions.description: Creates an iterator over a changeset buffer. Caller must finalize with sqlite3changeset_finalize().
requirements: pChangeset must point to complete changeset; iterator invalid after finalize.

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_start_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_start_v2(sqlite3_changeset_iter **pp, int nChangeset, void *pChangeset, int flags);
functions.description: Like sqlite3changeset_start, but flags (e.g., SQLITE_CHANGESETSTART_INVERT) can invert the changes during iteration.
requirements: flags must be a valid combination; otherwise SQLITE_MISUSE.

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_next
functions.description: Advances the iterator: returns SQLITE_ROW for next change, SQLITE_DONE at end, or error code. After error, iterator remains in error state.
requirements: Must have been created via start/start_v2; not the apply conflict iterator.

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_op
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_op(sqlite3_changeset_iter *pIter, const char **pzTab, int *pnCol, int *pOp, int *pbIndirect);
functions.description: Returns operation type (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE), table name, number of columns, and whether change was indirect for the current change.
requirements: pIter must be valid and positioned (next() returned SQLITE_ROW).
Output pointers must be non-NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_pk
functions.description: Returns an array marking primary-key columns for the current change (1 if part of PK, 0 otherwise) and number of columns.
requirements: Iterator must be positioned; output pointers non-NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_old
functions.description: Gets old.* value for column iVal of the current DELETE/UPDATE change. Sets *ppValue to protected sqlite3_value (or NULL for absent).
requirements: Iterator must be positioned on DELETE or UPDATE; iVal within range 0..nCol-1. Returns SQLITE_RANGE if invalid.
Value is valid until next iterator call or finalize.

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_new
functions.description: Gets new.* value for column iVal of the current INSERT/UPDATE change. May set *ppValue=NULL if column not modified in UPDATE.
requirements: Iterator must be positioned on INSERT or UPDATE; iVal within 0..nCol-1.
Protected value lifetime as above.

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_conflict
